articles.title: Cops rescue birds from wildlife trader in Bacolod City
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines — Law enforcement operatives led by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) arrested a 65-year-old man and rescued over a dozen birds during…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines — Law enforcement operatives led by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) arrested a 65-year-old man and rescued over a dozen birds during an entrapment operation in Barangay 30 here on Thursday, Sept. 3.
The suspect, identified by authorities only as alias “Ancheto,” was caught in a buy-bust sting operation.
He faces charges for the illegal possession and trading of wildlife under Section 27 of Republic Act No. 9147, otherwise known as the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act.

During the operation, operatives recovered marked buy-bust cash and boodle money, alongside 11 bird cages containing five Philippine Serpent Eagles, eight Martanico birds, two Green Parrots, two Coleto birds, a Grass Owl, and a “Sagaksak.”

The operation was led by the CIDG-Negros Occidental Provincial Field Unit and supported by the CIDG Bacolod City Field Unit, the Negros Occidental Maritime Police Station, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources–Community Environment and Natural Resources Office Bago City, and Police Station 6 of the Bacolod City Police Office. /cb

articles.title: Gatchalian extends aid to families of 3 Tacloban school shooting victims
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY, LEYTE, Philippines — The families of the three students killed in the June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School received financial assistance from Senate President Win…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY, LEYTE, Philippines — The families of the three students killed in the June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School received financial assistance from Senate President Win Gatchalian on Friday, September 4, as the Senate pushes legislation aimed at strengthening school safety nationwide.

Gatchalian’s staff personally delivered P50,000 each to the bereaved families of Chris Lorenz Fabian, Joyancee Separa, and Ayessa Nicole Dazo, who were killed when two fellow students opened fire inside the school campus.
The assistance was received by the victims’ families, including Christopher and Erbea Fabian, parents of Chris Lorenz; Jenelyn Badoria, mother of Joyancee; and Nico and Ariet Dazo, parents of Ayessa.
The Senate had earlier adopted a resolution expressing sympathy and condolences to the families of the three learners and providing P50,000 in assistance to each bereaved family.

The June 22 shooting claimed the lives of Fabian, Separa and Dazo and injured 20 others. Fabian, 15, a Grade 10 student and Boy Scout, was hailed for attempting to protect his classmates during the attack. Separa was also 15, while Dazo was 14.

The tragedy has since prompted calls for stronger security measures in schools and greater government attention to bullying, mental health, access to firearms and possible harmful online influences affecting young people.
Gatchalian said the Senate would continue pursuing measures designed to prevent similar incidents and strengthen the capacity of schools to respond to threats.
“We will focus on proposed laws that will promote the safety of schools. We will not allow violence that results in tragedy to happen again,” he said in a press statement.

Among the measures being considered by the Senate is Senate Bill No. 2426, or the Comprehensive School Safety Act, which seeks to establish a National School Safety Framework that would set standards for preventing, responding to and recovering from threats and incidents affecting school safety.

The proposed framework seeks a more comprehensive approach to school security rather than relying solely on physical measures, covering prevention, emergency response and recovery following incidents.

Government agencies have also provided continuing assistance to the victims’ families. The Department of Social Welfare and Development has extended financial and psychosocial support, while the National Housing Authority later provided housing units to the families of the three slain students.
The shooting also triggered broader discussions on juvenile accountability.

During a Senate hearing in July, Joyancee’s mother, Jenelyn Badoria, called for stronger accountability measures, including a review of the minimum age of criminal responsibility. The family of Ayessa also sought charges against the younger suspect.
The families have repeatedly called for justice and urged authorities to strengthen school security and prevent a similar tragedy from happening again.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. also honored Fabian, Separa and Dazo during his 2026 State of the Nation Address, describing their courage and selflessness as an inspiration to the nation. /cb

articles.title: London Paddington fire causes rail chaos as Heathrow trains cancelled
articles.summary:
Blaze causes electricity supply failure and disruption of services to airport and Reading

A fire near a train track in the London Paddington area has caused major disruption, with services…

blocks.text: A fire near a train track in the London Paddington area has caused major disruption, with services to Heathrow airport cancelled.
The fire caused an electricity supply failure which has left all lines between Paddington and the airport blocked, National Rail said.
Cancellations and delays to services are expected until 7.15pm, it added.
Photos on social media show large plumes of smoke rising from the Paddington area.
Great Western Railway (GWR) services to Reading have been cancelled, while the Elizabeth line is part-suspended.
No trains are running in either direction between Paddington and Heathrow, the Heathrow Express said.
The airport advised passengers to leave extra time for their journeys, adding that the Piccadilly line, which runs services to the airport, is also experiencing delays.

Transport for London (TfL) said the Elizabeth line is suspended between Paddington and Heathrow terminals four and five, and between Paddington and Reading, while the line to Abbey Wood is experiencing severe delays.
There are severe delays across the entire Piccadilly line due to an earlier trespasser at Hammersmith, according to the TfL website.
GWR said trains may be cancelled, delayed or terminated at and started back from Reading, with disruption expected until 7pm.
The London fire brigade has been contacted for comment.

articles.title: Egyptian TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death for drug crime
articles.summary:
Sarah Khalifa, 39, charged with forming organised criminal gang to manufacture and traffick drugs

An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for…

blocks.text: An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday.
The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.

The state-linked Al-Ahram newspaper said a Cairo court sentenced “Khalifa and 11 other defendants to death by hanging on charges of forming an organised criminal gang specialising in procuring materials used in manufacturing narcotics, with the intent to traffic them, and possessing and carrying unlicensed firearms and ammunition”.
The verdict came after the court consulted the Grand Mufti of Egypt for his religious opinion, a procedure required by Egyptian law in capital cases.
The verdict is subject to appeal.
Khalifa also owns a cosmetic surgery clinic and a production company that specialises in organising parties and events.

According to the state-run Akhbar el-Yom newspaper, the defendants were charged with “manufacturing synthetic drugs with the intent to traffic them, by importing the materials used in manufacturing from abroad”.
Al-Ahram reported that authorities seized more than 750kg of narcotics and raw materials, and found two apartments used as laboratories as well as unlicensed firearms and ammunition.
The court also sentenced Khalifa and others to five years in prison over a separate case involving the kidnapping and assault of a young man.
Egypt applies the death penalty for premeditated murder, terrorism, some rape offences and drug trafficking.
According to the Egyptian Commission for Rights and Freedoms, 541 death sentences were issued in Egypt in 2025.

articles.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
articles.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

image.caption: Tens of thousands of people attended the protest in ZagrebImage: AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A protest in Zagreb against Croatia's government drew tens of thousands of people who blamed the government for its lack of action over the illegal storage of toxic waste.

A landfill near the town of Gospic, located some 200 kilometers (124.2 miles) to Zagreb's southwest, is being used to hold toxic waste from several countries, including Germanyand Italy, according to reports.
The demonstration saw signs such as "ecocide equals slow genocide" and "halt waste import," with many of the people in attendance also holding Croatian flags.

The protesters called for all illegal landfills to be cleared due to them polluting groundwater, as well as a new waste management plan across the country within the next 20 days. They also demanded that the government put a temporary ban on waste imports in place.

blocks.caption: Protesters waved Croatian flags and demanded better waste managementImage: AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Investigation underway

An investigation in relation to illegal waste dumps has been ongoing since the arrests of 13 people in February 2025, with Europol cooperating with Croatian authorities in the investigation. Four companies are also under investigation.

According to Europol, most of the 35,000 tons of waste had come from Italy, but also from Slovenia and Germany, and consisted of plastic refuse and toxic hospital waste, bringing about a profit of some €4 million ($4.6 million) for the suspects, who had also likely forged documents falsely declaring plastic waste as suitable for recycling.
Local environmental activists dispute the number of waste tons and say 37,000 tons had been illegally dumped in Gospic alone.
Prosecutors also published a report in August that confirmed the Gospic soil contamination, also saying it had spread beyond the site itself.
This presents a "significant risk for the environmentand people's health," the report said, despite the drinking water in Gospic remaining so far unaffected, health authorities said.
Conservative Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic promised the toxic waste site in Gospic would be covered by mid-October before the waste gets removed from it.

articles.title: Wescom honors soldier slain in fight vs NPA in Palawan
articles.summary: PUERTO PRINCESA CITY, PALAWAN, Philippines — What was once a common household name for his family now marks a significant place in the history of the province of Palawan as the Armed Forces of the…

blocks.text: PUERTO PRINCESA CITY, PALAWAN, Philippines — What was once a common household name for his family now marks a significant place in the history of the province of Palawan as the Armed Forces of the Philippines’ Western Command (Wescom) celebrates the Staff Sergeant Cesar R. Barlas Day with the unveiling of a memorial marker at Mendoza Park last Thursday, Sept. 3, on the occasion of his sixth death anniversary, honoring him and the legacy he left behind.

Back in September 3, 2020, Barlas was leading a four-man team from the Marine 61st Force Reconnaissance Company in a combat operation in Sitio Cabuluan, Barangay Mainit of Brooke’s Point town when, at the break of day, they encountered a group of New People’s Army (NPA) rebels that resulted in an eight-minute firefight. Barlas was killed in the clash.

According to Maj. Gen. Vicente MAP Blanco, Philippine Marine Corps Commandant, the encounter “changed the course of Palawan’s history.” It was part of a series of operations conducted by Wescom through the 3rd Marine Brigade (3MBde) where five high-ranking NPA leaders were also killed, resulting in the group’s dismantling and the eventual declaration of Palawan as insurgency-free in 2023.

The AFP described Barlas’ actions as a sacrifice acting beyond the call of duty, and for such, he was awarded the Medal of Valor by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in December 2023, making him the first and only Palaweño so far to have received the highest award in military service.

Last 2025, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Palawan also recognized Barlas’ heroism through Resolution no. 21441 series of 2025 for his extraordinary courage during the encounter, displaying exceptional bravery and sacrifice that ultimately cost him his life.

During Thursday’s ceremony, Wescom chief Vice Admiral Alan Javier said the gathering was not just to unveil a memorial marker but to “remember a Filipino who gave the highest sacrifice in the service of his country.”

“Today we unveil a marker, but our greatest responsibility is to ensure that the memory and values it processes will not be forgotten. Staff Sergeant Barlas was the son of Palawan, a marine, a comrade, and a Filipino who answered the call of duty with extraordinary courage. His ultimate sacrifice earned him the medal of valor, a distinction that reflects the highest ideals of courage, gallantry, and selfless service,” Javier said.
“But today and this moment is not only about the medal. It is about the man behind the medal, the family behind the hero, the legacy behind the sacrifice,” he added.
Javier said that while it is part of a price that each member of the armed forces is willing to take, the service in uniform is also a commitment and sacrifice that the family of a soldier shares.
He said the SSgt. Barlas Memorial Marker will stand as a permanent reminder to every soldier of the commitment and principle that their uniform carries. /cb

articles.title: ‘I wasn’t even listening,’ Farage says of donations scandal meeting
articles.summary: Reform UK leader maintains innocence in overseas funding controversy on last day of party conference

blocks.text: Nigel Farage has claimed that he “wasn’t even listening” during a meeting at the centre of a controversy about whether his party considered evading the law on accepting donations from overseas.

The Reform UK leader also claimed that he knew donation law “better than anybody” during interviews as he sought to salvage the final day of his party conference from the fallout that has already cost him two of his closest aides.

Farage was forced to suspend his close aide Dan Jukes and Reform’s head of policy, James Orr, on Friday after they were filmed in an undercover investigation appearing to plot to get around electoral laws on foreign donations.

The undercover reporters from a group called Verbatim posed as a potential Reform supporter and his wealthy American father, an impermissible donor, who paid for £30,000 of polling commissioned by Reform and which benefited the party when it was published in national newspapers.

The Reform leader himself remains under pressure over a separate clip in which he was heard to say “it’s all above board” after one of the reporters who was posing as the UK-based son of a wealthy US backer told Farage he had been in discussions with Jukes and Orr for some time.
“I’ll be the registered donor,” the son says. “But then dad will send the money to me, and then as soon as that’s done and all those conversations are had the money is available.”

In an interview on Saturday, Farage told the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg that “of course” he knew it was illegal for foreign firms to donate to UK parties, adding he was told the money being givenvia a UK family office.

When challenged by Kuenssberg that while in Farage’s presence, one of the undercover reporters had said they “run an American family office”, the Reform leader said: “I am not a compliance officer. I was in the middle of canvassing in the Clacton byelection. I turn up. I frankly wasn’t even listening.”

He added: “I was told there was a global family office based in London, so the money could have come from Singapore. The money could come from all over the world, you know. Income could have come from all over the world into a family office based in London. I know electoral law. I know donation law better than anybody.”
Farage’s party had been hoping to move the focus to policy announcements, including on tax cuts, as Reform’s conference closed in Birmingham on Saturday.

Its Treasury spokesperson, Robert Jenrick, gave a keynote speech in which he pledged to increase the tax-free personal allowance to £15,000 within the first 100 days if the party were to take office. The threshold has been set at £12,570 since 2021 and is due to remain there until 2031.

But in interviews given earlier in the day to trail the policy, he also found himself forced to deflect from the donations controversy. “That’s been dealt with,” he told GB News. “The two individuals concerned have gone, and we’re here today moving forward. The language that they used was clearly inappropriate, that was very disappointing.”

In an interview with Times Radio he said Orr and Jukes had been “permanently suspended”, appearing to differ from the latest party line that they had “stepped down pending outcome of an investigation”, indicating a possible way back.
Farage meanwhile accused “the establishment” of trying to derail Reform UK, when challenged by ITV’s Robert Peston on the string of allegations related to his and the party’s finances.
“And it will go on. You come back and see me in six months, there’ll be five more investigations. It won’t end. This won’t end,” he said.
Farage said he had some “thoughtful” moments after over the summer, claiming his family had been asking him to “walk away” from politics amid pressure on them and him.
after newsletter promotion

Despite Reform’s efforts to insulate Farage, the Met police are now assessing evidence after a complaint that the Reform leader, as well as Orr and Jukes, may have broken political funding laws. They all deny wrongdoing.

The final day of the conference also coincided with an appeal by West Midlands police for a woman, who was among climate activists who were removed from the hall on Friday as they heckled Farage’s speech, to come forward after footage emerged over her allegedly being assaulted.

The police initially responded on X to a clip that appeared to show audience members pulling her hair and grabbing her head as she was carried out of the conference hall. West Midlands police later said in a statement that they were aware of a video circulating from the Reform UK conference showing an incident with a protester, and had asked the woman to come forward.
The activist group Climate Resistance, which claimed responsibility for the protest during Farage’s speech , said the protester was considering whether to speak to police.
Nadine Dorries, a former Conservative MP who has joined Reform, said sensitivities were “heightened” in the aftermath of the killing of the Reform spokesperson Anne Widdecombe in July.
“They tried to completely derail the speech. It was an organised sting again,” she said in an interview with LBC when asked about the incident.
Also speaking on Saturday was Suella Braverman, the party’s education spokesperson who, like Jenrick, is another defector from the Conservatives.

Her speech announced a planned cut of 20% to the number of student loans given, with funds only granted to university courses that can demonstrate good economic returns, with exceptions for some courses “of strategic or cultural importance”.

Farage ended the conference with closing comments to the main hall, where sections of seating were unoccupied and the mood was more subdued than earlier in the event, by telling the Reform faithful that “there would be good days and bad days”.

“Sometimes we will get things wrong and get a bit of a kicking, but what this conference has shown is that whatever you throw at the leadership, whatever you throw at you, the people’s army, we immediately stop, pick ourselves up and start all over again,” he said.

articles.title: Pulong Duterte insists Davao City got no congressional district budget
articles.summary: Davao City Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte on Saturday insisted that his hometown did not receive any congressional district allocation, disputing Palace Press Officer Claire Castro"s earlier…

blocks.text: Published September 6, 2026 12:17am

Davao City Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte on Saturday insisted that his hometown did not receive any congressional district allocation, disputing Palace Press Officer Claire Castro’s earlier statement that the government had provided funding to the city.
On Friday, Castro said Davao City received P52.80 billion in national tax allotment (NTA). Duterte, however, said this was different from the funding he was referring to.

“Ang NTA ay automatic appropriation para sa mga LGU (local government unit). Alam naman nating lahat iyan. Hindi ko sinabi na walang NTA ang Davao City…pero ang tinutukoy ko ay budget allocation para sa congressional districts,” Duterte said in a Facebook post.

(The NTA is an automatic appropriation for local government units. We all know that. I did not say that Davao City does not have an NTA. What I am referring to is the budget allocation for the congressional districts.)
Castro had cited the P52.80 billion NTA in response to Duterte’s allegation that Davao City had received no government funding.
“Sa sinasabing walang government funding na nilaan sa Davao City, ayon kay Cong. Pulong [Duterte], ito ang totoo,” Castro said.
(Regarding Cong. Pulong Duterte’s claim that no government funding was allocated to Davao City, this is the truth.)
Duterte said it would be best for the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) to show the records.

In a message to GMA News Online, Castro clarified that she had only been specifically asked about the NTA allotment, her assessment of the claim that Davao City had received no funds from the national government, and whether there were pertinent records to support the claim.

“It is better for the media to ask Pulong Duterte for those ‘proposed projects and their feasibility studies’ to see if the alleged denial of the congressional allocation was justified or not,” Castro said.
GMA News Online has also reached out to the DBM for comment and will update this story once it responds. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Zamora conducts consultations in Northern Mindanao, Caraga region
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — San Juan Mayor Francis Zamora, who is also national president of the League of Cities of the Philippines (LCP), conducted a two-day series of consultations with member cities in…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — San Juan Mayor Francis Zamora, who is also national president of the League of Cities of the Philippines (LCP), conducted a two-day series of consultations with member cities in Northern Mindanao and Caraga region on July 29 and 30, discussing priority national government programs and concerns affecting local governments while strengthening inter-LGU cooperation through sisterhood agreements between San Juan City and the cities of El Salvador, Gingoog, Bayugan, and Butuan.

The mission formed part of the LCP’s continuing nationwide consultations aimed at bringing the concerns of member cities directly to the National Government, particularly on the implementation of the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF), the Free Rice Distribution Program, the National Classroom Building Program, and other priority programs affecting cities across the country.
Misamis Oriental: El Salvador and Gingoog

The two-day mission began on July 29 at the El Salvador Little Theater, El Salvador City Hall, where Mayor Zamora met with local officials led by Mayor Edgar S. Lignes for the first LCP consultation of the trip.

Following the consultation, the City Government of San Juan and the City Government of El Salvador formalized a sisterhood agreement establishing cooperation in governance, tourism, education, disaster resilience, digital transformation, economic development, healthcare, sports, and other areas of mutual interest.

Mayor Lignes described the partnership as an important milestone for El Salvador City, saying it opens new opportunities to collaborate with San Juan in areas that directly benefit their constituents.

“This sisterhood agreement is an investment in our future. Through this partnership with San Juan City, we gain another trusted partner in public service, allowing us to exchange ideas, learn from each other’s successes, and pursue programs that will improve the quality of life of our people,” Mayor Lignes said.
In the afternoon, Mayor Zamora proceeded to the Penthouse of the Gingoog City Hall Complex, where he met with local officials led by Mayor Erick G. Cañosa for another LCP consultation.

The City Government of San Juan and the City Government of Gingoog subsequently signed their own sisterhood agreement aimed at promoting the exchange of best practices and strengthening collaboration between the two cities.
Mayor Cañosa welcomed the partnership, emphasizing the importance of cooperation among local governments.

“No city succeeds in isolation. By forging this partnership with San Juan City, we strengthen our capacity to innovate, improve governance, and deliver better services to our people. We look forward to building a lasting relationship founded on mutual respect, shared learning, and common aspirations for progress,” Mayor Cañosa said.
Mayor Zamora said the engagements in Misamis Oriental demonstrated how the LCP consultations and San Juan’s sisterhood initiatives complement each other in strengthening local governance.

“Every sisterhood agreement we sign is a commitment to move beyond friendship and toward meaningful collaboration. By sharing our experiences, innovations, and best practices, we strengthen not only our individual cities but also local governance across the country. At the same time, our LCP consultations ensure that the voices of our member cities are heard and reflected in national policies and programs,” Mayor Zamora said.
Caraga: Bayugan and Butuan
On July 30, Mayor Zamora continued the mission in the Caraga Region, beginning in Bayugan City, Agusan del Sur.

Before the LCP consultation, Mayor Zamora served as guest speaker during the city’s Nutrition Month Celebration at the Lope A. Asis Memorial Gymnasium. Addressing hundreds of students, teachers, nutrition workers, and local officials, the former athlete underscored the importance of proper nutrition, an active lifestyle, and making healthy choices.

Drawing from his experience in sports, Mayor Zamora encouraged students to develop discipline through proper nutrition and regular physical activity. He also cautioned the youth against illegal drugs, urging them to remain focused on their studies, pursue their passions, and become responsible citizens who will contribute to nation-building.
Following the program, Mayor Zamora proceeded to the Mayor’s Office Conference Room at Bayugan City Hall, where he met with Mayor Kirk Asis and local officials for the LCP consultation.

Mayor Zamora stressed that the continuing consultations strengthen the LCP as the collective voice of the country’s cities and provide local chief executives with a direct avenue for raising concerns with the National Government.

“As National President of the League of Cities, it is important that we continue listening to our member cities and serve as an effective bridge between local governments and the National Government. Every consultation gives us the opportunity to raise the concerns of our cities, follow up important national programs, and ensure that the voices of local governments are heard where decisions are made,” Mayor Zamora said.
Mayor Asis echoed the importance of the League’s role under Mayor Zamora’s leadership.

“Ang dami nang naitulong ni Mayor Francis sa lahat ng ginawa niya para sa 149 cities all over the country. Lahat ng follow-ups sa Malacañang at sa ating National Government, talagang tinututukan niya. Alam ninyo, bihira akong makakita ng isang mayor o president ng isang organization na katulad niya na talagang nagpa-follow up sa National Government para sa kapakanan ng local government units. He is our voice for the local government units. Sinasabi ko ito dahil ang mga ginagawa niya ay hindi lang para sa mga cities kundi para rin sa ating mga barangay. Ang mga benepisyong ipinaglalaban niya ay umaabot hanggang sa grassroots,” Mayor Asis said.

Following the consultation, Mayor Zamora and Mayor Asis formally signed the sisterhood agreement between the City Government of San Juan and the City Government of Bayugan at the Mayor’s Office Conference Room.

The agreement commits both cities to strengthen cooperation in governance, public service, tourism, education, healthcare, disaster preparedness, digital innovation, economic development, sports, and other areas of mutual interest while promoting the exchange of best practices for the benefit of their constituents.
The mission then proceeded to Butuan City, where Mayor Zamora toured the National Museum of the Philippines-Butuan and the Balangay Shrine Museum before proceeding to City Hall. /cb

articles.title: PDP-Laban denounces Sara arrest warrant
articles.summary: The Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Laban has denounced the issuance of a warrant of arrest against Vice President Sara Duterte, calling it an “assault” on the legitimate political…

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives at the Quezon City Hall of Justice on September 5, 2026.
Michael Varcas / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — The Partido Demokratiko Pilipino (PDP)-Laban has denounced the issuance of a warrant of arrest against Vice President Sara Duterte, calling it an “assault” on the legitimate political opposition.
It pointed to the fact that the arrest warrant was issued by a regional trial court judge recently appointed by President Marcos.

“The blatant attempt to decimate the political opposition is disingenuous yet obvious: appoint people beholden to the present administration to key positions in government agencies and use these agencies as weapons of mass harassment against those who dare oppose the prevailing corruption masterminded by the Palace,” PDP-Laban national spokesman Ferdinand Topacio said.
He urged the people to maintain their support “to the leaders of their choice” and resist the imposition of those that have been repudiated and “stand fast against the forces of dictatorship.”
However, House Deputy Speaker Paolo Ortega V said the issuance of the arrest warrant only means that Duterte should now confront the charges through the judicial process available to every accused.
Ortega said Duterte will have every opportunity to dispute the charges, question the prosecution’s evidence and avail herself of the remedies provided under the Rules of Court.

He said the development should therefore be allowed to proceed according to law, with the court ultimately determining criminal liability after hearing the evidence of both the prosecution and the defense.

For his part, Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon told Duterte to stop portraying her arrest as a threat to her safety and instead address the grave threats charges against her through the proper legal process.
Ridon made the statement after Duterte repeatedly expressed fears for her life after arriving at the Quezon City Hall of Justice yesterday to post bail.
Meanwhile, former press secretary Trixie Cruz-Angeles said Duterte’s supporters will remember the warrant of arrest against Duterte as oppression.
In a short video uploaded by Bilyonaryo News Channel, Angeles said, “History might not be a very kind judge because we will remember.”

“We will remember this, it is all on record and there will be people who would attest, there will be people who will stand with this, to all of these events and we’ll interpret them as oppression. So good luck in 2028,” she added. — Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: JV hopes reforms will boost Senate ratings
articles.summary: The Senate’s trust ratings will likely improve following reforms put in place by the new leadership, according to finance committee chairman Sen. JV Ejercito.

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Senator JV Ejercito on March 4, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — The Senate’s trust ratings will likely improve following reforms put in place by the new leadership, according to finance committee chairman Sen. JV Ejercito.
The senior deputy majority leader said the reforms include transparency measures in scrutinizing the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027.
Ejercito vowed to ensure that confidential funds are limited to government agencies with law enforcement and military mandate, including national security and the Office of the President.
“To avoid controversies, we will not give (confidential funds) to civilian agencies,” Ejercito said.
Agencies with lump sum budget items would be required to submit programs of work to ensure the funding goes to implemented projects and not lost to corruption.
“We will ask for all the details so we know how the funds will be used,” Ejercito said.
He hoped the Senate could redeem the public’s trust through reforms and prevent a repeat of the previous years’ budget insertions, which led to the flood control scandal.
Ejercito noted that the Senate ratings dropped while the House of Representatives improved.
He attributed the dip to the chaos that preceded the current leadership of Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian.
“It’s the first time in history that the Senate’s trust ratings are lower than the House. But hopefully, with the reforms in place, the Senate can regain the trust of the people,” Ejercito said.
He was reacting to the OCTA Research Group’s survey where the Senate’s ratings dropped to 41 percent in a survey conducted from July 4 to 11 from 44 percent in March.
Twenty-seven percent said they distrust the upper chamber, up from 24 percent, while undecided respondents remained at 32 percent.
The Senate’s performance ratings also dropped from 42 percent to 38 percent, with those dissatisfied with its performance increasing from 27 percent to 32 percent.
Undecided respondents hardly moved, from 31 percent to 30 percent.
The latest OCTA poll coincided with the start of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 6.

It captured the tumultuous Senate presidency dispute between Alan Peter Cayetano and Gatchalian, the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate and Sen. Ronald Dela Rosa’s escape, and the arrest of Sens. Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta on non-bailable plunder charges.
The House of Representatives’ trust ratings improved in the second quarter.
Thirty-eight percent said they trust the House, up from 36 percent, while 28 percent said they distrust it, down from 33 percent.
Undecided respondents increased from 30 percent to 33 percent.

In terms of performance, 37 percent said they were satisfied with the Lower House, up from 35 percent, while 32 percent were undecided, down from 35 percent. Those who were undecided hardly moved, from 30 percent to 31 percent.
OCTA’s second quarter survey had 1,200 respondents and a margin of error of plus/minus three percent. — Janvic Mateo

articles.title: DPWH working on detailed flood master plan
articles.summary: After the massive floods in Metro Manila and other provinces, the Department of Public Works and Highways is eyeing to create a science-backed flood management infrastructure plan to strengthen…

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Residents wade through floodwaters while others use paddle boats in a village in Lingayen, Pangasinan on August 30, 2026.
Cesar Ramirez / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — After the massive floods in Metro Manila and other provinces, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is eyeing to create a science-backed flood management infrastructure plan to strengthen long-term disaster preparedness in the country.
DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon has ordered the updating of all flood management master plans in the wake of the floods brought by tropical cyclones and the enhanced southwest monsoon.
He said they are laying the technical foundation for future flood control projects that are based on science.

The DPWH is collaborating with the University of the Philippines-Project Nationwide Operational Assessment of Hazards (NOAH), local governments and key partner agencies in the integration of hazard mapping and scientific data before the projects are implemented.
The DPWH is also working with NLEX Corp. for long-term solutions to ease the flooding at the North Luzon Expressway-San Simon Interchange in Pampanga.

Meanwhile, the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has directed its regional offices to coordinate with expressway managements for the timely dissemination on the status of the expressways within their respective areas of responsibility.
The directive covers Metro Manila, Ilocos Region where the TPLEX is located, Central Luzon where the SCTEX and NLEX is located and CALABARZON where SLEX, STAR Toll, CALAX and MCLEX are located.

Acting LTFRB Chairman Greg Pua Jr. said they also instructed all regional franchising and regulatory offices in the three regions to coordinate with the local government units in identifying alternative routes from the expressways in cases of emergency and other unexpected incidents similar to what happened at the San Simon area of NLEX.

“The incident that happened in NLEX is a wake-up call for us in the LTFRB and other agencies to do our part in coming up with measures to maximize the assistance to the public,” Pua said. — Josiah Antonio

articles.title: Impeachment unaffected by grave threats raps – Drilon
articles.summary: Former Senate president Frank Drilon said the grave threats case against Vice President Sara Duterte before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court has no bearing on her ongoing impeachment trial,…

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Former Senate president Frank Drilon said the grave threats case against Vice President Sara Duterte before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC) has no bearing on her ongoing impeachment trial, saying the two proceedings are different in nature.

Speaking to radio dwIZ, Drilon said the RTC case and impeachment trial tackle the same issue involving Duterte’s livestreamed statement that she had hired an assassin to kill President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez. However, he said the RTC case is criminal while the impeachment proceeding is political.

“As we have said, this impeachment trial is sui generis, a class of its own. It is not a court of law,” Drilon explained. “It is not a criminal case. It is a political process, a process provided for by the Constitution to hold accountable those who should be held accountable… The penalty here, if found guilty, is not imprisonment but removal from public office and perpetual disqualification from public office.”
Drilon also rejected claims that the grave threats case constitutes double jeopardy because the same allegations are being heard in the impeachment trial.
The alleged threats form part of Article IV of Duterte’s impeachment complaint. The prosecution has completed its presentation of evidence on the grave threats article.

Drilon said the criminal case under the Revised Penal Code requires a judge to find guilt beyond reasonable doubt, while an impeachment conviction requires a two-thirds vote of all senators based on their conscience.

“Not all senators are lawyers. Therefore, they cannot act as judges in determining whether there is proof beyond reasonable doubt. What matters is what is in their conscience, and that is what will prevail,” he said.
Drilon believes the impeachment court will render its verdict ahead of the RTC, with presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero saying the trial should be completed before yearend.
He added that there is no basis to believe that the impeachment court’s verdict would influence the RTC judge’s decision on Duterte’s grave threats case.

“The treatment or elements are different in the RTC and the impeachment court. So whether or not it will influence the judge is up to the court. It should not, but it is difficult to say because influence is a state of mind,” Drilon said. “That is a conclusion that has no basis.”
Drilon also disagreed with Duterte’s position that her assassination remarks were protected by freedom of expression.

“We have a law that prohibits threatening another person by telling them, ‘I will kill you.’ That is punishable under our Revised Penal Code,” he said. “Freedom of speech under our Constitution has limitations. You cannot invoke freedom of speech to threaten the entire country.”
Duterte posted bail at the Quezon City RTC in connection with the grave threats case filed by public prosecutors.
During the event, the Vice President invoked the memory of former senator Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino Jr. when she initially refused to enter the Quezon City Hall of Justice to post bail.
The court allowed media representatives to accompany her inside but required them to climb the stairs and stay at a distance from her.
Speaking in front of her lawyers Paul Lawrence Lim and Michael Poa, Duterte objected to the arrangement as she claimed threats against her life.
“Who will be at my back? Do you remember that Ninoy Aquino died on the stairs?” she said.
Aquino was killed on Aug. 23, 1983, at the tarmac of what was then the Manila International Airport after arriving from the United States aboard a China Airlines plane.
Duterte eventually entered the building, climbed the stairs and posted bail.
Face the case
House prosecutor Rep. Terry Ridon, meanwhile, challenged Duterte to stop the “drama” and face the legal process over the grave threats case.
Ridon said Duterte should not blame others for the case, stressing that the charges stemmed from statements she herself made.
“Enough with the drama. There would be no grave threats case if not for the statements that became the basis for the case filed against you,” he said.

The August Twenty-One Movement, meanwhile, described the arrest warrant against Duterte as a “step in the right direction,” although it said the development came as a surprise because the Philippines is known for a justice system that favors the powerful.

articles.title: ‘Prosecution focused on solid impeach case, not threshold’
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel is focused on presenting evidence strong enough to meet whatever conviction threshold will be adopted in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am

Defense counsel Atty. Michael Poa takes his oath as a hostile witness during the 21st day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on Sept. 2, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution panel is focused on presenting evidence strong enough to meet whatever conviction threshold will be adopted in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Prosecution counsel Benjamin Tolosa Jr. said they “never engaged” in vote counting and have yet to reach an official position amid proposals to review the 16-vote threshold for Duterte’s conviction.
“Our focus is whether it’s 16 votes or lower, we want to make sure that we get that number by laying down strong evidence,” he said.
The Constitution requires the concurrence of two-thirds of all Senate members for conviction. Presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero had interpreted this as 16 votes out of the 24 senators.
However, Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri recently said some senators want the threshold reviewed because some members could not attend the proceedings.
Tolosa said it’s not yet time for the prosecution to announce its position on the matter but added that the Senate could revisit its earlier “interim” ruling.
“My personal opinion is that it’s an interlocutory order which the senators can revisit,” he said, adding that interested parties could seek a Supreme Court review.
Tolosa said the prosecution’s work will continue while the senators try to address the issue.
“We want to establish an airtight case so whatever the interpretation is, we will meet the number,” he said.

articles.title: Online trolls target Quezon City judge
articles.summary: The Quezon City judge who issued the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte is now being targeted by trolls online.

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am
The doors of the Quezon City Hall of Justice were closed before 5 PM on September 4, 2026, as police officers secured the area and personnel from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) arrived.
Michael Varcas / The Philippine STAR
MANILA, Philippines — The Quezon City judge who issued the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte is now being targeted by trolls online.

Videos and images of Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 98 Judge Maria Angelica De Ramos are circulating on social media platforms, including Facebook pages dedicated to supporters of the Vice President.
Several posts have already drawn thousands of angry reactions, with many comments specifically targeting and disparaging the judge.
In addition to baseless allegations of corruption, trolls have also commented on the judge’s appearance and supposed ties with President Marcos.
Duterte’s allies and supporters, including former Commission on Elections commissioner Rowena Guanzon, have repeatedly pointed out that it was Marcos who appointed De Ramos to her post.
Members of the judiciary, despite being appointed by the executive, commit to independence and impartiality in carrying out their duties.

Under the existing process for judicial appointments, the President makes the appointment based on the shortlist submitted by the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC), an independent body that screens and vets nominees for vacant positions in the judiciary and other legal offices.
Records showed that De Ramos was among seven nominees shortlisted by the JBC for Branch 98 in July 2024. She was appointed in March 2025.
Security tightened
Police have tightened security in Metro Manila in anticipation of possible rallies by Duterte supporters.

Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano, National Capital Region Police Office director, said they have a contingency plan in place should Duterte’s supporters go on the streets to protest the cases against the Vice President. — Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: DepEd kicks off celebration of National Teachers’ Month
articles.summary: National Teachers’ Month is a time to thank, celebrate and prioritize the teachers, said Department of Education Secretary Sonny Angara.

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Teachers conduct their work at one of the teacher hubs in Batasan Hills National High School in Quezon City on June 26, 2025.
Michael Varcas / The Philippine STAR
MANILA, Philippines — National Teachers’ Month is a time to thank, celebrate and prioritize the teachers, said Department of Education (DepEd) Secretary Sonny Angara.
He was in Cagayan de Oro yesterday for the kick-off celebration of National Teachers’ Month 2026, which started yesterday and will run up to Oct. 5, with the theme, “Teacher, Ikaw Naman.”
In a statement, he thanked President Marcos for all his initiatives to improve teachers’ welfare.

“We thank President Bongbong Marcos for everything he has done for our teachers. If it is possible, our President would give it. That is also the philosophy of the Department of Education: to give what we could give to our teachers,” Angara said.
Addressing recent school safety concerns, the DepEd chief commended teachers for their dedication and willingness to go the extra mile, reinforcing the school’s role as a nurturing environment.

He said, “These times demand a lot from us. We are not only authority figures in schools. We should not forget that we also serve as their second homes,” adding that learners often just need to feel cared for.

“In this age of artificial intelligence, there will never be a substitute for a warm hug, a warm pat on the shoulder or even saying ‘hi’ and mentioning the name of our learners,” Angara added, reiterating that a whole-of-society effort is essential to support both educators and learners.

One of the activities of the celebration was corporate partner McDonald’s Philippines turning over 50 reclassified chairs – school furniture repurposed from retired restaurant assets – to East City Central School, alongside meal donations, interactive exhibits and raffle prizes for attendees.

The program concluded with a special video message from First Lady Liza Marcos who said, “As a teacher myself, I know the sacrifices you go through. I know about the patience, dedication and the heart to teach and inspire your students every day.”
The First Lady thanked the teachers for their unwavering commitment in helping shape the future of the nation.

DepEd had made policy reforms to improve working conditions nationwide, such as under the Expanded Career Progression (ECP) System, where DepEd promoted over 93,000 teachers and school heads and continues to create clearer professional pathways.
To reduce administrative stress, DepEd also slashed required regular school paperwork from 174 forms down to five, allowing teachers to focus on student instruction and mentorship.
Financial and medical benefits were also expanded. Under the Kabalikat sa Pagtuturo Act, the non-taxable annual teaching allowance doubled from P5,000 to P10,000.
Teachers now also receive an annual medical allowance of up to P7,000, five days of paid annual wellness leave and expanded vacation service credits capped at 30 days per year.

articles.title: Bonoan pleads not guilty to flood scam graft
articles.summary: Former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan has entered a “not guilty” plea before the Sandiganbayan Second Division on his remaining graft case concerning alleged kickbacks from flood…

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Former public works chief Manuel Bonoan arrives at the Sandiganbayan on Sept. 4 for the scheduled arraignment on his bailable graft charge over the flood control scandal.
Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — Former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan has entered a “not guilty” plea before the Sandiganbayan Second Division on his remaining graft case concerning alleged kickbacks from flood control projects.

Bonoan was arraigned on Sept. 4 after he was ordered released from police custody following his removal as co-accused in previous plunder and graft charges before the anti-graft court’s Fifth Division.
In this graft case, Bonoan’s co-accused is Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, who attended the arraignment via teleconference.
The charge stemmed from an alleged conspiracy to ensure the inclusion of flood control projects in Bulacan in the 2025 budget, where the senator allegedly received a P213.7-million kickback.
The anti-graft court division previously denied the prosecution’s move to have Bonoan excluded in the graft case but the former public works chief has filed an appeal to overturn this decision.

The court also entered a not guilty plea for Tarlac 3rd district Rep. Noel Rivera after he refused to enter a plea in his graft case over alleged conflict of interest in government infrastructure projects.

Ombudsman prosecutors have accused Rivera of having conflict of interest over his and his wife’s shares in Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corp., which bagged several government contracts while he was still congressman from 2022 to 2025.

Under Section 3.h of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, public officials are not allowed to have financial or pecuniary interest – directly or indirectly – in any business, contract or transaction in connection with which he intervenes or takes part in his official capacity, or in which he is prohibited by the Constitution or by any law from having any interest.
Rivera is facing nine counts of graft. One count each has been raffled to the First, Second and Fourth divisions of the anti-graft court, and two cases each to the Fifth, Sixth and Seventh divisions.

articles.title: MUPs to get 5% hike in base pay, allowances
articles.summary: The Marcos administration is opening its purse wider for the men and women in uniform next year, pairing a base pay increase with P350 daily subsistence allowances, as well as beefing up budget…

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am

Newly minted soldiers march in unison during the Pass in Review that marked the conclusion of their four-month Basic Military Training at the Makabulos Grandstand in Camp O'Donnell, Capas, Tarlac in this undated photo. T

MANILA, Philippines — The Marcos administration is opening its purse wider for the men and women in uniform next year, pairing a base pay increase with P350 daily subsistence allowances, as well as beefing up budget allocations for the military and police under the 2027 national budget.
The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) said more than 583,000 military and uniformed personnel (MUPs) are set to receive a five percent increase in base pay in 2027.

Acting Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon said the salary hike is part of the second tranche of adjusted base pay under Executive Order 107, which takes effect on Jan. 1, 2027. It was issued in December 2025.

The salary adjustment is being implemented in three tranches, beginning January 2026, followed by the second tranche in 2027 and the third in 2028. For the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), P74.92 billion is required for adjusted base pay, while P100.55 billion is provided for the Philippine National Police (PNP).

“For our total of 583,000 MUPs, P73.67 billion has been allocated specifically for the increased subsistence allowance for our MUPs, on top of the five percent increase in base pay that they can expect next year,” de Leon added.
For 2027, the executive branch is proposing P73.67 billion for the subsistence requirement of more than 583,000 personnel. Of this amount, P30.71 billion is proposed for 246,844 AFP personnel.
Bigger budgets
The pay adjustment comes alongside higher spending on military and police operations, modernization and manpower.

The AFP is proposed to receive P316.71 billion in 2027, 6.9 percent higher than its 2026 budget. Of this, P50 billion is earmarked for the Revised AFP Modernization Program, up from P40 billion this year.

The DBM said the government is pursuing personnel welfare and modernization as complementary parts of the same defense strategy. “Modern equipment is essential amid evolving security challenges, but so are well-trained, properly compensated and adequately supported personnel who will operate these capabilities,” it added.

De Leon said the government is likewise increasing resources for AFP Personnel Services, Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) and capital outlays to strengthen the capability of troops to fulfill their mission and defend the country’s sovereignty.
On the other hand, the PNP is also set to receive a larger allocation, with its proposed 2027 budget rising to P242.53 billion from P226.55 billion this year.

About P210.55 billion of the proposed allocation will go to personnel services, including the P100.55-billion funding for adjusted base pay and P28.67 billion for the P350 daily subsistence allowance of 224,421 PNP personnel.

The government is also setting aside P697.18 million for the hiring of 2,000 additional patrolmen and patrolwomen, while P2.19 billion is proposed for filling currently unfilled uniformed positions. The proposed budget also provides P1.74 billion for rice subsidy, P280.67 million for hospitalization and health care of police personnel and their dependents and P125.11 million for the Bantay Kaisipan Health Program.
For police operations and equipment, the government is proposing P2 billion for the PNP Capability Enhancement Program, which covers mobility, communications, firepower and anti-terrorism equipment.
Another P3.12 billion is earmarked for information and communications technology, while P1.5 billion is proposed for infrastructure projects.

articles.title: Pilandok to reenter PAR
articles.summary: Tropical Storm Krovanh, formerly known as Pilandok, is expected to reenter the Philippine area of responsibility tomorrow morning or early afternoon, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and…

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 12:00am
As of 4 p.m. yesterday, Krovanh was located 830 kilometers northeast of extreme northern Luzon, packing winds of 65 kilometers per hour and gusts of up to 80 kph.
PAGASA

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Storm Krovanh, formerly known as Pilandok, is expected to reenter the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) tomorrow morning or early afternoon, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said.
It was moving southeastward at 25 kph over the coastal waters of Okinawa, Japan, state meteorologists said.

“Once inside PAR, the tropical cyclone will be given its former local name Pilandok,” PAGASA said. “While moving eastward over the Philippine Sea, it will shift northeastward and exit PAR by Monday before turning northward toward southern Japan.”
PAGASA said Pilandok will maintain its tropical storm category until Monday before weakening into a tropical depression on Tuesday.
While landfall and direct weather or sea effects remain unlikely, the state weather bureau said the storm may enhance the southwest monsoon in the next few days.
Occasional rains brought by the southwest monsoon will be experienced in Metro Manila, Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Laguna, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro.
The Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Western Visayas, Abra and Benguet will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms.
The southwest monsoon will bring partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms to the rest of Luzon and the Visayas.
Meanwhile, partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms are expected in Mindanao due to localized thunderstorms.

articles.title: US military says it struck three Iranian tankers after American warships came under missile attack
articles.summary:
Officials said US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided attacks before three Iranian tankers were struck by the US

The US…

blocks.text: The US military said Saturday it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US navy warships came under missile attack, further escalating tensions in the region and warning it would “if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet”.
According to the military, a US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks” while patrolling the region. No US personnel were injured.
Two of the Iranian oil carriers were “permanently disabled”, the Pentagon said, while a third tanker, which was unladen, was destroyed.
The US said the vessels were part of a shadow network that helped finance Iran’s powerful Revolutionary Guards and armed proxy groups operating across the region.
“We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet,” the head of US Central Command, Adm Brad Cooper, said in the statement.

The announcement followed an earlier report from Iran that the US had attacked an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island in the Gulf. Tasnim, a semiofficial news outlet affiliated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, reported the strike happened on Saturday morning. It said the tanker’s crew survived and was being evacuated.

The US said one tanker was struck off Kharg Island, while another was hit near Jask. The unladen tanker was struck in the Gulf of Oman. The US statement also shared what it described as video footage of the strikes.

The latest attacks came nearly a week after the US and Iran resumed strikes after about a month of relative calm in the on-again, off-again war that began with US and Israeli attacks in February. Attempts at negotiations have collapsed.
One of the strikes hit a wedding in southern Iran on Tuesday, killing four people, including a child, and injuring dozens, according to Iranian officials.
The US vice-president, JD Vance, said “sometimes things happen” when asked on Thursday whether an US strike was responsible for killing people at the wedding celebration.
after newsletter promotion
The renewed strikes have also brought fresh scrutiny to a 28 February US attack in Minab that struck a school compound and killed at least 156 people, most of them schoolchildren.

A preliminary US military inquiry reportedly found that the attack resulted from a targeting error after outdated coordinates identified the school as part of a nearby Revolutionary Guards naval base. The Pentagon said at the time that it was investigating. A full report has not been made public.
Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: U.S. ambassador visits Palestinian town amid rise in occupied West Bank settler violence
articles.summary: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee on Saturday met with Palestinian Americans, including relatives of U.S. citizens killed by Israeli settlers, in a Palestinian town in the occupied West Bank…

image.caption: Mike Huckabee, the U.S. ambassador to Israel, speaks to reporters on Saturday after meeting residents of Turmus Ayya, a Palestinian town near Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank that is home to many American citizens. (Ammar Awad/Reuters)

blocks.text: World

U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee on Saturday met with Palestinian Americans, including relatives of U.S. citizens killed by Israeli settlers, in a Palestinian town in the occupied West Bank that has been the target of settler attacks.
About 80% of Turmus Ayya's roughly 3,000 residents hold U.S. citizenship, mayor says
The visit comes as settler violence — and what is widely perceived as the Israeli government's inaction — has increasingly drawn international condemnation, including from U.S. allies.
The Israeli government has condemned settler violence, though perpetrators are rarely arrested and even less frequently prosecuted.
Washington has not criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government over the violence, but it has called for perpetrators to be prosecuted, with Huckabee labelling them as terrorists.
The ambassador described his meeting in Turmus Ayya, where most of the town's Palestinian residents are U.S. citizens, as constructive.

items: Mike Huckabee, U.S. ambassador to Israel, condemns 'horrific' violence in West Bank

blocks.text: While Huckabee, a Baptist minister and longtime supporter of Israeli settlements, has previously called for violent settlers to be prosecuted, he also says he believes they represent a minority of the settler community, which numbers about 750,000.
About three million Palestinians live in the occupied West Bank, with tens of thousands estimated to be American citizens.

Palestinians in the West Bank have faced a surge in settler violence while their freedoms have been increasingly curtailed under military occupation since Netanyahu's coalition — the most right wing in Israel's history — came to power in late 2022.

In Turmus Ayya, Palestinians are facing what Mayor Nawwaf Zaghoul said were constant settler attacks. About 80 per cent of the Palestinian town's roughly 3,000 residents hold U.S. citizenship, he said.
Visits to Shiloh
Israeli settlements have been established around the town, including Shiloh, which the ambassador has visited twice since 2025.

Huckabee, the first evangelical Christian to serve as U.S. envoy to Israel, refers to the West Bank as Judea and Samaria, its biblical name, which is used by the Israeli government but has not been adopted by the United States.

Huckabee told reporters in Turmus Ayya that it was in the Israeli government's interest to take action against those carrying out "criminal behaviour and terrorism" and that a "tiny group of little marauders," who he said numbered a few hundred people, were damaging the country's reputation.

He also said he had told Palestinian Americans that the U.S. Embassy had no power or authority to take action and could only seek to influence and call attention to issues that the U.S. government believed needed to be corrected.

In January 2025, shortly after returning to office, U.S. President Donald Trump rescinded sanctions imposed by the Biden administration on far-right Israeli settler groups and individuals accused of being involved in violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

Yasser Alkam, a Palestinian American and a municipality spokesperson, disagreed with Huckabee's characterization that only a few hundred settlers were carrying out violence against Palestinians. There were thousands, he said, not hundreds.
U.S. ambassador condemns Israeli settlers' siege of Palestinian homes in West Bank

"The United States does have the power to pressure Israel, at least arrest these settlers, which are known to the authorities," Alkam told reporters. "They can identify them, one by one, and arrest them, if they want to, with the right amount of pressure from the United States Embassy and the United States administration."
Among those who met Huckabee on Saturday was Hadeel Jabara, a Palestinian American mother of two young children whose husband, Omar, a U.S. citizen, was killed by settlers in 2023.
She described the meeting as positive, adding she hoped the U.S. government could help protect residents and that she feared for her children's safety.
At least six Palestinian Americans have been killed in the occupied West Bank either by the Israeli military or settlers since 2024.

articles.title: Sara Duterte to Remulla, PNP: ‘We do not trust you’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday once more stressed her lack of trust in the police and Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, whom she described as…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday once more stressed her lack of trust in the police and Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, whom she described as subservient to the administration.
“Wala kaming tiwala sa iyo, Jonvic Remulla, at sa mga pulis na sunod-sunuran sa isang korap na pamahalaang pinamumunuan ni Marcos,” in a statement posted on Facebook.
(“We do not trust you, Jonvic Remulla, nor the police who are subservient to a corrupt government led by Marcos.”)
Duterte’s remarks were made after Remulla said he and the Philippine National Police (PNP) knew her whereabouts amid an arrest warrant issued to her by the Quezon City Regional Trial Court (QC RTC).
Remulla said they decided not to implement the warrant of arrest despite knowing her location the night before.
The Vice President said his pronouncement only proved the Marcos administration’s surveillance operations and harassment against her.
She further cited the PNP as among the government agencies involved.

“Ang mga salitang ito ni Secretary Jonvic Remulla ay tila nagpapatibay sa mga dokumentong matagal na naming hawak hinggil sa harassment at surveillance operations ng Philippine National Police at iba pang ahensya ng gobyerno laban sa akin,” she insisted.

(“These statements by Secretary Jonvic Remulla appear to corroborate the documents I have long held regarding the harassment and surveillance operations conducted by the Philippine National Police and other government agencies against me.”)
The Vice President even questioned how police personnel came for her family after allegedly locating her.
“Isa lamang ang malinaw na sagot—upang takutin at sindakin ang aking pamilya,” she said.
(“There is only one clear answer—to frighten and terrorize my family.”)
Duterte said that, while she recognizes the jurisdiction of the PNP, she still won’t surrender herself out of fear for her safety.
She said that the authorities cannot guarantee that she will be protected while in detention and in police custody.

“Higit sa lahat, huwag nating kalimutan ang ginawang pagkidnap ng Philippine National Police kay Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte. Pati na rin sa marami pang ginagawang harassment ng pulisya sa mga sibilyan,” she added.
(“Above all, let us not forget the kidnapping of President Rodrigo Duterte by the Philippine National Police, as well as the many other acts of harassment committed by the police against civilians.”)
Duterte further said government funds should be used to pursue and convict criminals, including public officials who accept suitcases containing the people’s money.
The Vice President posted bail early Saturday at the QC RTC for three counts of grave threats, where she told the media her worries regarding her and her family’s security.
The case stemmed from Duterte’s alleged death threats to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., first lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez in 2024. /cb

articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, ILOCOS SUR, Philippines — Three people were arrested for allegedly engaging in an illegal card game in Barangay Laslasong Norte, Sta. Maria in this province on Friday (Sept. 4), police…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, ILOCOS SUR, Philippines — Three people were arrested for allegedly engaging in an illegal card game in Barangay Laslasong Norte, Sta. Maria in this province on Friday (Sept. 4), police said.
Personnel of the Sta. Maria Municipal Police Station, led by Lt. Jenson Refuerzo, officer in charge, acted on an intelligence report about an ongoing gambling activity in the village.
Police caught the three suspects in the act while playing “tong-its,” resulting in their arrest for alleged violation of Presidential Decree No. 1602, or the law penalizing illegal gambling.
Gambling paraphernalia seized from the suspects were inventoried and marked at the scene in the presence of two barangay officials and the arrested individuals.
Police said the operation was documented using two authorized recording devices in accordance with PNP rules and procedures.
The suspects were brought to the Ilocos Sur District Hospital in Narvacan for medical examination. —KENNETH P. TABIN/CONTRIBUTOR

blocks.text: DARAGA, ALBAY, Philippines — Fifty-four barangays in this town have been equipped with rescue vehicles worth a total of P78 million to improve emergency response and disaster preparedness in their communities.

The vehicles, funded through the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF), were blessed by Rev. Fr. Tony Cial and turned over Friday (Sept. 4) during a ceremony at the Municipal Nursery in Barangay Gabawan led by Mayor Vic Perete and Ako Bicol Party-list Rep. Alfredo Garbin Jr.

Perete said the vehicles, equipped with fire extinguishers and other emergency equipment, would allow barangays to respond to emergencies and other incidents without having to rely solely on the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO).

“We aim for zero casualty. May these rescue vehicles serve as a symbol of our continuing commitment to protect lives, strengthen disaster preparedness, and provide faster and more effective emergency response to the people of Daraga,” he said.
Perete thanked President Marcos and Ako Bicol party-list for helping facilitate the project and secure funding for the vehicles. /cb

articles.title: U.S. military hits 3 Iranian oil tankers after saying its navy warships were targeted
articles.summary: The U.S. military on Saturday said it struck three Iranian oil tankers after navy warships were targeted with missiles, warning that it would "if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil…

image.caption: Commercial vessels lie anchored in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran on Friday. The U.S. military said Saturday it struck three oil tankers, including one east of the Strait of Hormuz. (Vahid Salemi/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

The U.S. military on Saturday said it struck three Iranian oil tankers after navy warships were targeted with missiles, warning that it would "if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet."
Military says aircraft carrier, destroyer evaded 'multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks' while on patrol

The strikes — a day after U.S. President Donald Trump sought to minimize the conflict as "small potatoes" — keep up a new tilt back toward fighting after six months of on-again, off-again war that began with U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran on Feb. 28. Both sides have sought to inflict both military and economic pain, and negotiations have collapsed.

The military's statement said a U.S. aircraft carrier and a destroyer evaded "multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks" while patrolling in the region and no U.S. personnel were hurt. It said two Iranian oil carriers were "permanently disabled" and the third, unladen one, was destroyed.
The U.S. statement said the tankers were part of a shadow network helping to fund Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guard and its armed proxies in the region.

Earlier, Iranian state TV had said four U.S. missiles struck a tanker about 10 kilometres from Kharg Island, home to a terminal through which the country exports most of its oil. Kharg Island been repeatedly targeted during the war, including U.S. strikes on military sites there in March.
Iran targets American bases after accusing U.S. of deadly strike on wedding

The U.S. said one tanker was struck off Kharg Island and another was struck near Jask, east of the Strait of Hormuz. The unladen tanker was hit in the Gulf of Oman. The statement shared what it called video footage of the strikes.
"We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet," the head of U.S. Central Command Adm. Brad Cooper said.
Hostilities flare

The strikes came nearly a week after the U.S. and Iran resumed attacks following a month of relative calm, with the strait and Iranian communities along it again being targeted. At least five people were killed earlier in the week during a U.S. bombardment of southern Iran. One strike hit a wedding.

items: Day of attacks by U.S. and Iran marks most serious escalation of conflict in weeks
Iran attacks U.S. bases across Gulf after reports of deadly strike on wedding

blocks.text: The resumption of fighting came after new U.S. efforts to apply economic pressures on Tehran, whose hard-line new senior leaders have signalled the willingness to dig in after weathering decades of sanctions.

Meanwhile, the issue that helped lead to the war — Iran's nuclear program — was meant to be addressed in negotiations that fell apart soon after the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in mid-June. Instead, Tehran's new leverage focuses on the strait that is crucial to global oil and natural gas shipments and was seen as an international waterway before the war began.
The U.S. military has been helping to guide ships through the strait as Tehran asserts control and targets some vessels, but overall traffic remains low.
