articles.title: Ilocos Sur town forms task force vs illicit tobacco trade
articles.summary: CALASIAO, PANGASINAN, Philippines — The municipality of San Ildefonso in Ilocos Sur has officially created a local task force to strengthen its campaign against illicit tobacco and vapor products.…

blocks.text: CALASIAO, PANGASINAN, Philippines — The municipality of San Ildefonso in Ilocos Sur has officially created a local task force to strengthen its campaign against illicit tobacco and vapor products.
The Local Anti-Illicit Trade Task Force will improve intelligence sharing, coordinate enforcement efforts and strengthen the capacity of local personnel to combat the illegal trade.

Municipal Ordinance No. 06-2026, approved on Wednesday (Sept. 2), builds on an earlier executive order issued by Mayor Amante “Tito” Purisima and establishes a permanent framework against the sale, distribution, transport, storage and possession of noncompliant or counterfeit tobacco and vapor products.

Local officials said the measure is particularly important because of Ilocos Sur’s strategic location and proximity to areas where illicit trade activities may emerge, including parts of Central Luzon.
The Ilocos Region has also emerged as a hotspot for illicit cigarette trading, based on Philippine National Police seizure records during the first half of 2026.

At a recent Tobacco Summit organized by the National Tobacco Administration, the PNP reported the seizure of an estimated P20 million worth of illicit cigarettes in Region I during the first six months of the year.
Widespread
A San Ildefonso resident also said vaping had become widespread in the town, particularly among students.

The ordinance was enacted following consultations with local stakeholders on the economic and social effects of illicit tobacco trade, including losses in government revenue, unfair competition against legitimate businesses and its impact on community welfare.
It defines illicit products as those without required government registrations, internal revenue stamps or graphic health warnings, as well as those sold below the minimum price prescribed by law.

Businesses will be required to comply with anti-illicit trade regulations as a condition for the issuance and continued validity of their permits. Violations may result in the suspension or revocation of permits, while major or large-volume cases may be referred to national authorities for possible action under existing laws.

The ordinance also calls for a registry of violators, training for enforcement personnel, public information campaigns, annual implementation reports and regular assessments of the municipality’s anti-illicit trade efforts.
With the new measure, San Ildefonso joins a growing number of local governments taking a more active role against illicit tobacco trade.

Mariveles, Bataan, earlier issued Executive Order No. 008-S-2026, establishing a coordinated anti-contraband enforcement framework, while Caloocan City enacted an ordinance strengthening inspections, business accountability, and coordination with national enforcement agencies. /cb

articles.title: Raise the Colours leader given access to Reform UK conference while on bail
articles.summary:
Ryan Bridge, arrested this year on suspicion of religiously and racially aggravated harassment, says party invited him

The leader of a flag campaign group who was arrested on suspicion of…

blocks.text: The leader of a flag campaign group who was arrested on suspicion of causing religiously and racially aggravated harassment was given access to Reform UK’s annual conference.
Ryan Bridge, whose Raise the Colours group has put up hundreds of union and St George flags across England, told the Guardian he was invited to the conference.
Raise the Colours has argued the campaign displays flags as a sign of patriotism, but it has been accused of using them to spread anti-immigrant sentiment.

Bridge’s attendance at the event comes as Reform UK has been attempting to attract more wavering centre-ground voters who have been reluctant to support the party. But a threat from its hard-right rival Restore Britain has given the party reason to pull rightwards.

At a conference event on Saturday, Nigel Farage paid tribute to the flag campaign and told Bridge personally that Reform UK would offer legal support. “What your campaign has done is wake up vast parts of this country,” Farage told Bridge from a stage inside the conference after the activist was among three people selected to ask questions of the Reform leader during a discussion hosted by Jeremy Kyle.
“If we can help you legally, we will,” said Farage, after Bridge told him he had an injunction against him putting up flags in Oxfordshire and was also facing one from Birmingham city council.
Bridge was among 10 activists who were banned from France this year after they travelled there to take part in actions intended to stop migrant boats embarking across the Channel.

He is also named along with six other people in action pursued by Birmingham city council as it seeks a high court injunction to stop activists from Raise the Colours putting flags up. The first hearing of that application will be on Tuesday.

Bridge has been on bail since Thames Valley police confirmed earlier this year that a 44-year-old male from Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, was arrested after reports of incidents of public order offences on Abingdon Road, Oxford. The force said he was arrested “on suspicion of causing racially and religiously aggravated harassment, alarm or distress” and that he had been released on police bail. Bridge denies all wrongdoing.

He is also facing a trial in East Sussex. He entered a not guilty plea at Brighton magistrates court last month after being charged with common assault in relation to an incident in the city in June and was granted bail.

Bridge told the Guardian at the Reform conference on the outskirts of Birmingham on Friday: “We have come to the event today in light of it’s in my home city of Birmingham and with what’s going on with Raise the Colours … what we are doing.”
“We got an invite, so we thought we would come along,” he added, saying he was not a member of Reform.

There are no general admission tickets to the Reform conference for members of the public. Conference attenders are almost entirely members, with the addition of some lobbyists, people with business interests, diplomatic representatives and members of the press. Commercial passes can be bought for £650 and “platinum” tickets can cost thousands.

Asked if his arrests posed a problem with him being at the event, Bridge said: “Being accused of a criminal act of raising a flag of your country in your country, I think is lesser than the actual criminal act that is going on on a daily basis from the far-left ultra NGOs.”
Reform UK did not respond when contacted about Bridge being at its conference.

His attendance was criticised by the anti-fascist campaign group Hope Not Hate, which said: “That someone as extreme as Ryan Bridge was inside the Reform conference with a pass is genuinely shocking.”

articles.title: US hits three Iranian oil tankers after saying its warships were targeted
articles.summary: US Central Command says the attacks came after Iran launched ballistic missiles at two of its Navy warships.

blocks.text: The US military says it has hit three Iran-linked oil tankers after ballistic missiles were launched towards two of its warships in the region.
US Central Command (Centcom) said on Saturday it had "permanently disabled" a tanker near Kharg Island and another near the Strait of Hormuz, and "completely destroyed" a third in the Gulf of Oman.

Centcom said it "successfully evaded" multiple attacks from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeting a US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer. No American troops were harmed, it said in a statement.
Iranian state media earlier reported that one of its oil tankers had been struck by US missiles off the coast of Kharg Island.
"Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost - taking out three of yours," said Admiral Brad Cooper, Centcom's commander.
"We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet."
The strikes come nearly a week after renewed attacks between the US and Iran, which followed a month of relative calm between the warring sides.

The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic.

articles.title: Solon pushes for bigger DOH budget in 2027 after massive cuts
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio on Saturday slammed the planned cuts to the Department of Health’s (DOH) budget amid medical personnel…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio on Saturday slammed the planned cuts to the Department of Health’s (DOH) budget amid medical personnel shortages.
Under the 2027 National Expenditure Program, the health agency received a significantly lower-than-requested budget of P353.8 billion from its proposed P837 billion for next year.

During the House committee on appropriations’ briefing on the DOH’s 2027 proposed budget, Tinio raised that the massive budget reduction would affect the fund intended for hospital operations and personnel services.
The solon cited that DOH hospitals in Metro Manila would receive only P26.9 billion from the previous P30 billion in 2026.
He noted that Rizal Memorial Medical Center would have a half-billion-peso loss, while the National Center for Mental Health gets a P311-million cut.

“Kulang na nga ng staff, binabawasan pa. The DOH itself admitted these are unfilled plantilla positions being removed from next year’s budget. That means hospitals will have no opportunity to fill them up during the fiscal year,” Tinio expressed.

(“There is already a shortage of staff; it is being reduced. The DOH itself admitted these are unfilled plantilla positions being removed from next year’s budget. That means hospitals will have no opportunity to fill them up during the fiscal year.”)
He expressed that filling vacant plantilla positions would address the problem of insufficient medical personnel and professionals in public hospitals.
Tinio then called for the restoration of the proposed cuts in the personnel services and maintenance and other operating expenses (MOOE) of DOH-retained hospitals.

Although the DOH said it would obtain additional funds through Philippine Health Insurance Corp (PhilHealth) reimbursements and allocations in the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) program, it will still be insufficient to sustain the needs of hospitals.

Primarily, only 30,000 hospital beds remained authorized, despite the “promised expansion” of 45,000 by 2028—which was delayed because of the Health Facilities Enhancement Program budget cuts, according to Tinio.

“But reimbursement is not instantaneous. In the meantime, our hospitals will be operating on funds that are insufficient—and patients will suffer. Ang kailangan ng mga ospital, direct na pondo para direktang maibigay ang serbisyo,” he stressed.

(“But reimbursement is not instantaneous. In the meantime, our hospitals will be operating on funds that are insufficient—and patients will suffer. What hospitals need is direct funds to directly provide the service.”)
He continued, “We oppose this arrangement na mukhang pinagkakasunduan ng DBM at DOH na bawasan ang MOOE ng mga ospital dahil daw may MAIFIP at PhilHealth.”
(“We oppose this arrangement—which the DBM and DOH appear to be agreeing upon—to reduce the hospitals’ MOOE, supposedly because of the existence of MAIFIP and PhilHealth.”
He said that he would take these concerns to the plenary in a bid to seek bigger funding for the DOH.

“Maganda ang Zero Balance Billing sa papel, pero kung limitado ang kapasidad ng ating mga pampublikong ospital, limitado rin ang makikinabang na mamamayan. Iiwanan lang ng sistema ang ating mga kababayan sa mga pribadong ospital na mas mahal,” he said.

(“Zero Balance Billing looks good on paper, but if the capacity of our public hospitals is limited, the number of citizens who can benefit from it is also limited. The system will simply leave our fellow citizens to rely on private hospitals, which are more expensive.”)

articles.title: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner land in Moscow aiming to revive Ukraine talks
articles.summary:
US envoys expected to meet Vladimir Putin before going to Kyiv, after peace efforts floundered in recent months

The US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to try to…

blocks.text: The US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to try to resuscitate a deal to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as both sides said they would halt airstrikes for the visit.

The envoys were met at the airport on Saturday by the Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, a key interlocutor for the Trump administration’s efforts to end the Ukraine-Russia war. The US outlet Axios reported that they were expected to meet the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, later in the day.

The visit came as Trump suggested on Friday a new proposal to end the war, without providing any details on what his new plan might be. Trump made ending the war a priority early in his second term, but his efforts have so far yielded little results.

“I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They’ve done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it,” Trump said.

The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said Kyiv would stop its airstrikes during the US officials’ visit and asked Moscow do the same. The Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said on Saturday that Putin had ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv.

Large gaps remain between Russia and Ukraine on how to end the war. On Friday, the Kremlin said it was sticking by the position Putin set out two years earlier – that Ukraine should give up four regions claimed by Russia and not join Nato. That position is intolerable to Ukraine.

Witkoff and Kushner were expected to visit Kyiv on Sunday, which would be the first time the two envoys have visited the Ukrainian capital. Both have visited Moscow before, their latest visit in January when they met Putin in the Kremlin.

As peace efforts floundered in recent months, with US attention turned to its war with Iran, the conflict has intensified. Ground troops have been locked in a grinding stalemate along the 775-mile (1,250km) frontline with little advances on either side. Both sides have intensified their aerial attacks in recent weeks, hitting increasingly distant targets.

Ukraine has carried out long-range strikes on Russian military facilities, oil refineries and e-commerce warehouses, to try to degrade Russia’s war-effort and economy. Its strikes on Russian oil refineries have led to fuel shortages and rising prices at the pump.

On Friday, a Russian drone hit the headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU), one of the agencies which are responsible for carrying out deep-strike operations in Russia. Zelenskyy has vowed to retaliate. Russia has also increased its attacks on Kyiv and other cities with waves of bombardments, stretching Ukraine’s air defence systems.

Zelenskyy accused Russia of trying to disrupt the envoys’ visit to Ukraine with strikes on Kyiv’s two airports overnight. “Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine,” Zelensky said in a post on X.
Officials visiting Ukraine have largely done so by train, as Ukrainian airspace has been closed since 2022 due to the war.

On Friday, Russia carried out overnight strikes, killing five people and wounding five more at a factory in the southern Dnipropetrovsk region, according to thje local military administration head, Oleksandr Hanzha. He said those killed were employees working at the factory who were “doing their job when enemy missiles cut off their lives.”
A 62-year-old man was wounded and several homes and a building were damaged in an another attack on the region’s Nikopol district, Hanzha said.

Russia also struck a shopping centre in the southern Mykolaiv region with drones overnight, damaging the building and wounding a 72-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl. Emergency services said they were repeatedly forced to withdraw because of the threat of more strikes.
Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched ballistic missiles and 167 drones overnight, including jet-powered UAVs. Ukrainian air defences disabled 128 of the drones, the air force said.
Russia’s defence ministry said it had shot down 53 Ukrainian drones overnight.

The boy was found at the top of Mt. Mabitog in Sitio Asilip, Barangay Caganayan, around 11 a.m., during continuing search and rescue operations conducted by local responders and volunteers.

articles.title: Cut the cameras: Flock surveillance cameras spur rare bipartisan backlash
articles.summary:
Politicians on the right and left are pushing back against Flock as more Americans voice opposition to the tech

Growing factions from both sides of the political aisle in the US are pushing…

blocks.text: Growing factions from both sides of the political aisle in the US are pushing back against surveillance cameras made by a single company, a rare response in a sharply divided country with a president pushing an unwaveringly pro-tech agenda.

The bipartisan backlash against Flock Safety cameras resembles nationwide rage toward the construction of large datacenters that power artificial intelligence. Polling shows roughly 75% of Americans oppose new datacenter construction in their areas.

Flock’s cameras are automated license plate readers (ALPRs), which take pictures of vehicle license plates so police and security companies can log the movement of cars in a given area. There are about 120,000 Flock cameras across the US, which conduct roughly 2bn scans per month. The company is staring down controversy after reports of abuses of its cameras by police officers in multiple states, who have used them to stalk ex-lovers and track people seeking abortions. The network the cameras feed into is also frequently utilized by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Data and polling from the Washington Post show that social media posts about Flock have increased since July, and about 46% of Americans oppose ALPRs being used in their community – up 13 points from the previous year. Vigilantes are posting videos of themselves destroying the cameras to digital applause. According to privacy and surveillance experts, hatred of Flock cameras has become bipartisan.

“In my 20-plus years at the ACLU, I’ve never really seen such a grassroots uprising against surveillance technology like this,” said Jay Stanley, a senior policy analyst at the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU). “On the left, there’s a historical memory of law enforcement spying on and interfering with advocates for social change … On the right, there’s a long tradition of ‘don’t tread on me’ – keep the government out of my life, keep it from looking over my shoulder.”

Both liberal and conservative politicians are pushing back against Flock cameras. Greg Abbott, Texas’s Republican governor, blocked state agencies from procuring Flock products. On the other side of the political spectrum, Bernie Sanders, the progressive US senator, is promising to introduce legislation to restrict the use of Flock cameras. Republican senator Josh Hawley has launched an investigation into potential Flock privacy abuses, and Democratic congressman Ro Khanna is cosponsoring a bill with Republican congressman Thomas Massie to prevent federal funds from being used to purchase Flock cameras.

Municipal leaders of all political stripes are dropping contracts with Flock, though sometimes they replace the license plate readers with another brand of camera and continue the surveillance. We reached out to Flock Safety for a statement and did not receive a response before publishing.

Surveillance hasn’t always been a unifying topic in US politics. Debates over the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (Fisa), the Patriot Act and other surveillance issues have often been divisive. This appears to be an unusual case where politicians are getting on the same side of a hot-button issue.

“Privacy, to some extent, is bipartisan,” said Matthew Guariglia, a senior policy analyst at the Electronic Frontier Foundation. “When you put up these cameras, they last longer than the current administration. You might trust the people in power now who put them up – but are you going to trust the next people who get access to that equipment?”

Americans have been showing up at town hall meetings by the dozen over the past six months or so, and there have been numerous protests to show opposition to Flock surveillance cameras around the country. More than 100 jurisdictions have canceled their contracts so far, according to data from the non-profit Institute for Justice. An organization called DeFlock, founded in 2024, hopes to increase the numbers by compiling a map of the cameras’ locations.

While ALPRs aren’t new, Flock, founded in 2017, has made them far more prevalent than they used to be. The company’s software allows disparate law enforcement agencies to share data with one another, meaning a license plate scan by a police department in one state could easily and quickly be used in another.
after newsletter promotion

“Flock represents tech companies in bed with governments, doing the exact stuff people have become distrustful of and resentful about for the past few decades. It feels like it’s finally hit the boiling-over point,” said Woodrow Hartzog, a professor of law and computer science at Boston University.

Hartzog predicts the actions against Flock Safety will continue at the state and local level amid this growing popular outrage. He expects people are going to stay angry about the issue, and politicians will have to respond.

“The pushback we’re seeing against Flock cameras is one of the most vivid illustrations I can think of that surveillance is not inevitable – that these tools aren’t inevitable,” Hartzog says. “It’s up to all of us to stop them.”

articles.title: Masked anti-migrant protesters block UK's Dover terminal
articles.summary: Chanting "stop the boats" and wearing balaclavas, the demonstrators blocked traffic at the UK's busiest international ferry port.

image.caption: Police said they eventually moved the masked protesters onto trains out of Dover portImage: Oscar Rihll/PA Wire/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Hundreds of masked people blocked traffic at England's port of Dover on Saturday as part of an anti-migrant protest, halting ferry traffic between France and the UK.
Video footage showed demonstrators in balaclavas chanting "stop the boats," in a reference to refugees and migrants who attempt the dangerous English channel crossing in a bid to reach Great Britain.

This came despite the fact that crossing dropped 40% between January and August 2026 compared to the previous year. However, the perceived threat of migrant boats has become a rallying cry for the far-right Reform UK party.
Police said that they were "engaging" with protesters and that normal traffic had resumed at the port after several hours.
Government condemns 'travel disruption'

"The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but we condemn the behavior in Dover and the travel disruption it has caused," said a spokesman for the government of Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
Under Burnham and his predecessor Keir Starmer, migrant crossings have been greatly reduced in part due to closer cooperation with French authorities.
Dover is the UK's biggest international ferry port, handling some 15,000 passengers a day during the summer and welcoming more than a third of the UK's trade goods with the European Union.

articles.title: Fact check: Germany's postal voting system isn't rigged
articles.summary: As Germany heads into three elections in September, rumors are circulating on social media claiming that postal voting is not secure — claims that have also been made about other elections. Here's…

image.caption: Postal voting has become a target for fraud allegations in Germany, as it has in other democracies, including the USImage: Revierfoto/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Stakes are high in Germany's three September state elections. In Saxony-Anhalt, where voters go to the ballot boxes on Sunday, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) could make history in by winning an outright majority.

The AfD's Saxony-Anhalt branch, which has been classified by the domestic intelligence agency as a "confirmed right-wing extremist organization", could become Germany's first far-right state government since World War II.

Mail-in voting, or "Briefwahl," has become an increasingly common feature of German elections. But the rise in mail-in ballots has been followed by a renewed wave of speculation and claims questioning the security and integrity of postal vote.
DW Fact check examined a sample of claims circulating online and assessed what the available evidence shows.
Does postal voting manipulate election results?
Claim: Cases of fraud involving postal ballots prove that postal voting is unreliable.
This claim recurrently appeared in posts about postal voting that DW Fact check reviewed on social media platforms including TikTok, X and Facebook.

Some posts point to individual cases of electoral fraud involving postal ballots and present them as evidence that the system as a whole is flawed. One verified account on X using the AfD logo, for example, cited two cases — a mail-in vote being cast on behalf of an elderly woman with dementia, and hundreds of voters in Magdeburg receiving multiple ballots — before calling postal voting defective and demanding immediate reforms.

blocks.caption: Social media is rife with posts like this one on X, which cited individual problems with mail-in ballots as evidence that postal voting is fundamentally unreliableImage: X/AfD

blocks.text: DW Fact check: Misleading. Individual cases of fraud, errors or violations do not demonstrate that the entire postal voting system is unreliable or that it has affected the outcome of an election.

The post by the X account with the AfD logo refers to two real incidents, but does so in a misleading way. The claim about an elderly woman may refer to a case in Dessau, where police recently investigated an alleged vote cast on behalf of a 95-year-old woman with "severe dementia" but found no evidence of manipulation. The other incident occurred in Magdeburg, where 440 voters did receive duplicate ballots for the September 6 election ; however, the duplicates were invalidated and could not be used to cast additional valid votes.

Cases of electoral misconduct involving postal ballots have occurred in postal voting, as they have with voting at polling stations. In one case in Dresden, a man manipulated absentee ballots during the 2024 local and state elections, primarily in favor of the far-right Free Saxons party as well as the AfD. And in Bavaria, a former mayor was accused of manipulating postal voting documents in a March 2026 local election.

There have also been documented mistakes, administrative problems and delays in the handling of postal ballots in previous German elections. A 2021 study examining postal voting in German federal elections between 1998 and 2017 found that these weaknesses were primarily related to organization and logistics. Researcher Daniel Hellmann of the Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg said, however, that the research was still ongoing.
But such problems are not evidence of widespread fraud or of postal ballots being manipulated on a scale capable of changing an election result.
The 2021 study concluded that postal voting in Germany was secure overall. It found that none of the incidents examined could have changed an election result by even a single seat.

"If problems have occurred, they have generally been reviewed through legal channels and proportionate consequences have been imposed," Lukas Stötzer, an election researcher at the University of Witten/Herdecke in western Germany, told DW. "The postal voting system works and is secure, and that's why it is becoming more popular."

blocks.caption: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD's lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund has called for postal voting to be restricted to justified exceptional cases. But officials have defended postal voting as a secure and established procedureImage: Annegret Hilse/REUTERS

blocks.text: Postal voting easy to manipulate?
Claim: Postal votes are easily manipulated during counting.

"It can be assumed that postal voting in Saxony-Anhalt will massively distort the election result, This is also relatively easy to do, and the checks on postal voting are laughable," wrote one user on X with about 130,000 followers on August 14.

blocks.caption: Some posts have argued that postal votes are easier to manipulate during the counting processImage: X

blocks.text: This claim was also a recurring theme among the posts reviewed by DW Fact check, with some of the content presented in satirical, AI-generated cartoons. The AI-generated video depicted here on TikTok and labelled satire, for example, shows a man involved in counting ballots simply altering the votes from AfD to the center-right CDU party, and then calling a man named "Friedrich" — presumably Chancellor Friedrich Merz — to say that he had "everything under control."

DW Fact check: False. Germany has detailed procedures governing the handling and counting of postal ballots. Postal votes are transported, stored and opened according to established rules, and their counting takes place publicly.

Members of the public are generally allowed to observe the election process, including the counting of votes, without having to demonstrate a particular interest or affiliation. This applies to postal ballot counting as well.

That means election officials do not simply open postal ballots and count them behind closed doors. The process is conducted by election boards, whose work can be observed by members of the public and each parties' representatives.

blocks.caption: In Germany, eligible voters can be called upon by local authorities to serve as election workers and are generally required by law to accept the roleImage: ABBfoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: In an interview with German public broadcaster ARD Christa Dieckmann, Saxony-Anhalt's state election commissioner, pointed to public observation as an important safeguard. "The best way to ensure the fairness of the election is to come to the polling station as an observer for elections as the basis for choosing a legitimate government," she said.

DW Fact check also encountered numerous claims promoting what has been dubbed the "nursing home theory," which alleges that elderly people who are unable to vote in person may not be casting their ballots freely, but could instead be pressured or influenced by certain political parties or caregivers.

DW Fact check has investigated similar claims in the past, many of which have been promoted by AfD politicians. It has found no substantial evidence to support the broader allegation that postal voting in nursing homes is systematically manipulated or that elderly voters are routinely pressured into voting for particular parties.
A familiar claim beyond Germany

The doubts surrounding postal voting are not unique to Germany. Similar claims have surfaced during elections in other democracies, often becoming entangled with broader political battles over the legitimacy of elections.

During the 2020 US presidential election, President Donald Trump repeatedly claimed that expanded mail-in voting would lead to widespread fraud. Fact-checkers documented and debunked repeated false and exaggerated claims about the security of mail ballots. Ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, the Trump administration is again seeking to impose new restrictions on mail-in ballots, measures that have faced repeated legal challenges.
Fact-check: The truth on burned votes
Election researcher Stötzer said such claims can become part of a broader political strategy to undermine trust in democratic institutions.
"Right-wing populist parties strategically fuel these doubts," Stötzer said, adding that such claims can later be used to justify electoral law changes that benefit those parties.
He said the immediate impact of such allegations may be limited. But if they are repeated election after election, the longer-term consequences could be more serious.
"Public trust in electoral institutions could suffer," Stötzer said. Election results that are considered undesirable could then routinely be attributed to alleged irregularities in postal voting.
This is a collaborative project between ARD-faktenfinder, and DW Fact check.

articles.title: Civilians among at least 60 killed in Yemen as ground fighting escalates
articles.summary:
Houthi rebel offensive against government forces on west coast leads to some of deadliest clashes in years

Clashes between Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi…

blocks.text: Clashes between Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi rebel movement have killed more than 60 people, including civilians, as the Houthis pushed forward with a military offensive on Yemen’s western coast.

Twenty-six government troops and 31 Houthi fighters were killed during several hours of fighting in the country’s south-west on Saturday, medical and military sources told Agence France-Presse (AFP). A missile strike also killed six civilians and injured seven others travelling by bus in the city of Taiz.

The killings were the latest in a series of bloody clashes in recent days as the Houthis continued an offensive in western Taiz and southern Hodeidah along the Red Sea coast. On Friday, 129 were killed in fighting between rebel and government forces, according to an AFP tally.

The fighting is some of the deadliest in years, after the collapse in July of the 2022 ceasefire. The truce fell apart after an Iranian plane attempted to land in Houthi-controlled Sana’a, triggering attacks by the Yemeni government on the airport.

The Houthis are trying to beat back governmental troops to capture strategic hills overlooking Bab al-Mandeb in order to advance towards port cities on the coast. So far, they have managed to capture areas in western Taiz.

In Taiz, a government military officer said the “coming hours will be decisive” as the Houthis had taken positions near the city a day before. They added that reinforcements had been arriving from Aden to try to stem the Houthi advance.
On Friday, government forces said that they had recaptured the al-Khazan and al-Makahna hills west of Taiz, two strategically important areas for controlling the region.
The Houthis had previously controlled the port city of al-Makha overlooking Bab al-Mandeb, before being pushed out by government forces backed by the Saudi-led coalition.

The Bab al-Mandeb strait is a crucial maritime chokepoint for ships heading to the Suez canal. About 10% of global maritime trade passes through the strait. Saudi Arabia has been using the strait to export oil for months after the start of the US-Iran war.
If shipping is disrupted in Bab al-Mandeb, it will only further raise the cost of global goods, which has already rocketed as a result of the virtual closure of the strait of Hormuz since March 2026.

If the Houthis manage to recapture the port city and take key areas along the Red Sea coast, it will help them control naval traffic in the Red Sea. In July, the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia, and they have repeatedly disrupted traffic in solidarity with Gaza since the start of the war there in October 2023.

Yemen has been embroiled in a civil war since 2014, when the Houthis and allied forces took the capital city of Sana’a and pushed the then government out of power. A Saudi-led coalition then began a military intervention to support the Yemeni government and fight the Houthis, a strategic ally of Iran.

At least 150,000 people in Yemen have been killed in the fighting, and hundreds of thousands more have died from related causes such as hunger and diseases. About 4.5 million people have been displaced by the fighting and more than 18.2 million are in dire need of humanitarian assistance, according to the UN.

articles.title: Ombudsman urges SC to act on complaint vs. 7 CA justices over TRO
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday called on the Supreme Court to act on a complaint filed last year by former Ombudsman Samuel Martires against seven Court of Appeals (CA) justices for…

blocks.text: Published September 5, 2026 9:46pm

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday called on the Supreme Court to act on a complaint filed last year by former Ombudsman Samuel Martires against seven Court of Appeals (CA) justices for alleged gross ignorance of the law.
In a radio program on Saturday, Remulla said his office was responding to the Supreme Court’s challenge to file complaints over alleged misconduct in the judiciary.
“Ang ginagawa namin ngayon, iniipon namin lahat ‘yung graveyard namin ng mga reversed cases and TROs issued. Sa admin ito. So iniipon namin ‘yan, ipa-publish namin ‘yan,” he said.
(What we are doing now is collecting all the reversed cases and TROs issued in administrative cases. We are compiling them and will publish them.)
GMA News Online sought the side of the Supreme Court for comment and will update this story once a response is received.

Remulla recalled that Martires filed the complaint on March 21, 2025, against Associate Justices Louis Acosta, Marlene Gonzales-Sison, Rex Bernardo Pascual, Mary Charlene Hernandez-Azura, Roberto Quiroz, Rafael Antonio Santos, and Ferdinand Baylon.
The former Ombudsman accused the CA justices of alleged gross ignorance of the law and conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service.
The complaint stemmed from the justices’ issuance of a temporary restraining order (TRO) against a preventive suspension order involving eight members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Antique.
“To date, there appears to be no public record of the Judicial Integrity Board or the Supreme Court having acted on or resolved the complaint,” Remulla said.
Remulla underscored his office’s mandate to inform the public about such cases.

“We will also inform them of everything, but we will also inform the public. Since you're inviting us to file the complaints, we will also inform the public. It's our duty to inform the public of these things that have happened,” he said. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong
articles.summary: As the UN adopts a new world map to reflect Africa's true size, let's take a closer look at what different maps get right and wrong.

blocks.text: The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University London College explained.

"He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC. "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well."
To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are, with countries nearer the poles appearing stretched.
The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.

But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
"Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.

articles.title: PNP: VP Sara has not reported threats, harassment
articles.summary: Philippine National Police chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said Vice President Sara Duterte has yet to report to the PNP any threat against her and her family. Nartatez said this in a…

blocks.text: Published September 5, 2026 9:31pm
Philippine National Police chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said Vice President Sara Duterte has yet to report to the PNP any threat against her and her family.
Nartatez said this in a statement hours after Duterte said that she had been receiving threats and harassment since 2023, the year she broke away from the Marcos administration.
She added that she feared for her children.
Nartatez said the PNP said it has taken note of the concerns raised by the vice president, vowing that it would monitor the situation.
"To date, however, the Vice President has not reported to the PNP any threat to her life or to the safety of her family, including the threats she said date back to 2023," Nartatez said.
"Likewise, the PNP has not monitored any verified threat against the Vice President or her family," he added.
Nartatez also said the police provided security to Duterte when she posted bail. She was able to safely arrive and leave the court.
"The PNP remains open to receiving any document, report, or statement concerning the reported threats," Nartatez said.
Duterte on Saturday posted bail at a Quezon City court, a day after the issuance of an arrest warrant against her over her grave threats case.
The QC Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 98 set the bail at P120,000 per count. It found that there is probable cause to hold Duterte for trial, prompting it to issue an arrest warrant against her.
Shortly before she posted bail, Poa told reporters that Duterte was considered "surrendered."
GMA News' Jonathan Andal quoted Duterte's counsel Paul Lawrence Lim as saying the vice president did not have her mugshot taken inside the courtroom.
She took the stairs to and from the QC RTC-Branch 98 inside the Hall of Justice, saying she wanted to be seen by the media amid her security concerns.
In a statement, Duterte said she does not feel safe.
"I have documented threats and harassment since 2023. I fear for my children. I do not feel they are safe if I am with them," she said.
"Umalis na nga ako kung nasaan mga anak ko para pumunta sa korte pero pumunta pa rin ang pulis," Duterte added.
"I do not feel safe. Pakiramdam ko papatayin nila ako," the vice president said.

Duterte did not appear before the Quezon City court on Friday, the day that the warrant was issued. Additional police forces had been deployed at the Hall of Justice, with cops bringing inside the building a backdrop used for taking mugshots.
Policemen were securing the area on Saturday as well. Poa and Lim arrived at the Hall of Justice ahead of the vice president.

To recall, the DOJ filed three counts of grave threats against the vice president over her remarks that she hired an individual to kill President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former speaker Martin Romualdez, should an alleged plot against her succeed.

Following this, Duterte filed a motion to quash on the ground of jurisdiction, arguing that she and other impeachable officers have limited procedural immunity while in office under the 1987 Constitution.
The court held the oral arguments on Duterte’s motion in late August.
For her part, Duterte previously said her remarks were "maliciously taken out of logical context."
The vice president's alleged grave threats against Marcos is also the basis of one of the Articles of Impeachment against her in the ongoing trial before the Senate impeachment court. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: PCG probes yacht’s routes after P366M kush haul in Subic Bay
articles.summary: OLONGAPO CITY — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Saturday (Sept. 5) said it is seeking access to the sailing yacht ‘Lindsy’ to examine possible clues on maritime routes used to…

blocks.text: OLONGAPO CITY — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Saturday (Sept. 5) said it is seeking access to the sailing yacht ‘Lindsy’ to examine possible clues on maritime routes used to transport illegal drugs into the country.
The boat is currently in the custody of the Bureau of Customs (BOC).
Cmdr. Euphraim Jayson Diciano, head of the PCG in Zambales, told the Inquirer that they had sent a letter to BOC-Port of Subic District Collector Geniefelle Lagmay requesting access to the yacht.
The Coast Guard wants to examine the watercraft as part of its ongoing investigation.

Diciano said the PCG will check the yacht’s voyage history, movements and navigational data to identify patterns and possible maritime corridors that may have been used to transport illegal substances.
Among the equipment and records the PCG wants to see are the yacht’s logbooks, navigational charts and onboard navigation systems.
These pieces include the boat’s electronic chart display and information system (ECDIS), chart plotter, global positioning system (GPS) and automatic identification system (AIS).
“These records will be examined to help authorities establish the yacht’s voyage history, including its movements before it arrived at Subic Bay,” Diciano said in a phone interview.
The Coast Guard said information gathered from the examination can also be incorporated into its database for future maritime law enforcement operations.
The request came as authorities continued to investigate the yacht following the discovery of alleged high-grade marijuana, or “kush,” on board the vessel at the Subic Bay Yacht Club (SBYC).
Authorities have yet to determine whether the yacht’s navigation records can establish its previous movements or shed light on possible routes connected to the shipment of illegal substances.
The total value of the suspected high-grade marijuana recovered from the yacht reached P366.6 million after authorities continued stripping and searching the vessel.
The BOC-Port of Subic confirmed on Saturday that its composite team found 109 additional packages of kush worth an estimated P204.4 million.
Authorities searched different compartments and hard-to-reach areas of the vessel, including its underside.
“Coast Guard divers also went underwater to inspect portions of the yacht as part of the continuing search for possible hidden contraband,” Diciano said.
The initial seizure followed information received by the PCG Intelligence Unit-Zambales on Sept. 1.
Mechanics repairing the yacht’s generator and engine reportedly discovered a hidden compartment containing suspected illegal substances.
This incident prompted authorities to hold covert verification and prepare an operation with the BOC and Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA).
On Sept. 2, authorities boarded and searched the yacht, recovering approximately 89 bags of suspected kush weighing 98.3 kilograms.
The yacht arrived at the SBYC on Aug. 28 after encountering generator and engine problems while sailing from Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia to Taiwan. /apl

articles.title: Putin orders 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv as U.S. envoys visit Russia and Ukraine
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv, the Kremlin said Saturday, as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow to try to revive a stalled…

image.caption: Firefighters try to extinguish a blaze at a partially destroyed warehouse after a Russian drone attack in Brovary, on the outskirts of Ukraine's capital Kyiv, on Friday. (Francisco Seco/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv, the Kremlin said Saturday, as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow to try to revive a stalled push to end Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Last known visit to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner was in January

"Putin has ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight today," presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russia's Tass news agency. He said the decision was tied to preparations for Witkoff and Kushner's planned visit to the Ukrainian capital, which Kyiv has said will take place on Sunday.

The envoys' trip comes as both sides escalate aerial attacks, some four and a half years after the Kremlin's invasion of its neighbour. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Friday that Ukraine would halt airstrikes during the envoys' visit and urged Moscow to do the same.

items: Trump says Witkoff, Kushner heading abroad in latest U.S. effort to end Ukraine war

blocks.text: Washington’s push to end the fighting, now in its fifth year, has lost momentum as U.S. attention has been focused for the last six months on its war with Iran.
The last known visit to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, was in January, when they met Putin in the Kremlin. They have never previously visited Kyiv.

The Americans were met at the airport by Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev, Tass reported. Dmitriev shared photos of him meeting the U.S. delegation as they disembarked, alongside the caption, "Welcome to Moscow Peacemakers."

items: Russian attack hits Ukraine's security service headquarters
Carney prepared to tell Putin to 'get out of Ukraine' if Russia welcomed to G20 summit

blocks.text: With peace efforts stalled, Russia has intensified its attacks on Kyiv and other cities with relentless bombardments recently stretching into daylight hours, taking advantage of Ukraine's shortage of air defensive systems.

On Friday, a Russian drone hit one of the most important government buildings in Kyiv — the headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service, known as the SBU, which is one of the agencies involved in carrying out deep-strike operations inside Russia.

The long-range strikes by Ukraine have hit Russian military facilities, oil refineries and e-commerce hubs, seeking to undermine the Kremlin's war effort and economy, as well as make ordinary citizens feel the consequences of the war.
Intelligence warns Putin is preparing escalation in Ukraine
Zelenskyy links Russian strikes to envoys' visit

The air war between Russia and Ukraine has intensified as troops have struggled to make progress along the 1,250-kilometre front line. Russia has recently been using fast-flying, jet-powered drones, and the recurring wail of air-raid sirens has become part of daily life in Kyiv.
In a social media post on Saturday, Zelenskyy said Russia had carried out overnight strikes on the Kyiv and Boryspil international airports, and he linked the attack to the planned U.S. visit.
"Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the U.S. side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine," he said.

"We have taken note of this Russian move, and next week we will adjust our operation accordingly regarding Russian airspace, which has become dangerous because of our drones and missiles in the sky. Of course, there are and will be no threats to diplomacy from our side."
Strikes kill 5 at Ukrainian industrial site

Russian attacks killed five people and wounded five more at an industrial facility in Ukraine's southern Dnipropetrovsk region, local military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha said. He described those killed as employees at the site.

"A locksmith, an electrician, a plumber and a machinist. People of peaceful professions. They were simply working their shift. They were doing their job when enemy missiles cut off their lives," he said.
A 62-year-old man was wounded and several homes and an apartment building were damaged in a separate attack on the region's Nikopol district, Hanzha said.
See the aftermath of Russian strikes on warehouses around Kyiv

In a statement on Saturday, Russia’s Ministry of Defence said it had carried out strikes on two metallurgical plants in the region, describing them as "major suppliers of metal products for Ukraine's military production."

A further two people were wounded in an overnight Russian attack on Ukraine’s Kyiv region, said Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional military administration. In the Boryspil district, a fire sparked by a strike partially destroyed a nine-storey residential building.

Russian forces also repeatedly struck a shopping centre in the southern Mykolaiv region with drones overnight, damaging retail premises and sparking fires, Ukraine's state emergency services said. A 72-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl were hurt.

items: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expected to visit Canada next week: sources

blocks.text: Emergency crews responding to the incident were repeatedly forced to withdraw to safety because of the threat of further strikes, returning whenever conditions allowed, the emergency services said.

Russia launched ballistic missiles from its Rostov and Voronezh regions and deployed 167 attack drones overnight, Ukraine's air force said. The drones included Shahed-type aircraft — about half of them jet-powered — as well as Geran and decoy drones. Ukrainian air defences shot down or suppressed 128 drones, according to the air force.

Elsewhere, Ukrainian attacks wounded three people, including a 14-year-old girl, in Russia's border region of Belgorod, local officials said. In a statement, Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces had shot down 53 Ukrainian drones overnight.

articles.title: Russia to pause strikes against Kyiv amid Ukraine talks
articles.summary: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Moscow to revive Ukraine peace talks. The trip is the pair's first visit to Kyiv since US President Donald Trump's reelection.
articles.byline: Zac Crellin, Nik Martin, Sean Sinico

image.caption: US special envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on SaturdayImage: REUTERS

blocks.text: Russia will pause strikes against Kyiv for three days, the Kremlin said on Saturday, coinciding with peace negoatiations led by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Russian President Vladimir Putin "has ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight today," Kremlin spokesperson Dmirty Peskov told state media.
It comes after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy already committed to pausing airstrikes for the talks.

"As with previous diplomatic visits by the American side, we will ensure the normal functioning of Russian airspace so that the negotiators can arrive safely. We are concerned about their safety, not about Russia," Zelenskyy said.
Kushner, Witkoff arrive in Moscow
The US envoys Kushner and Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Saturday. They were met at the airport by Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev.
Hours earlier, US President Donald Trump said he was sending his son-in-law Kushner and businessman Witkoff to Moscow and Kyiv with a proposal to end the conflict.

"They're bringing with them a proposal to end the war," Trump told reporters Friday when asked about the pair's trip. Kushner and Witkoff have served as Trump's envoys to lead peace efforts in the Middle East as well as Ukraine.

The US president did not provide any details on the potential plan, including whether it involved Ukraine giving territory to Russia as he has previously suggested. Instead, he said, "We have an idea for peace."
US envoys to visit Kyiv next
Zelenskyy announced earlier on Friday that Kushner and Witkoff would visit Ukraine on Sunday following talks in Moscow.

Recent media reports have questioned whether the pair would indeed travel to Ukraine. Despite trips to Moscow to meet with Russian officials, the US envoys have not visited Kyiv since Trump's reelection last year.

Trump had promised to end the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year, on his first day back in office, but has more recently said that the feat was more complicated than expected. In the past, he has blamed Ukraine for the Russian invasion and a "personality problem" between the countries' leaders for the continued fighting.

blocks.caption: Kushner and Witkoff met with Russia's Putin (left) in January; they have not been to KyivImage: Alexander Kazakov/Sputnik/Kremlin Pool Photo via AP/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Drone strikes continue
Meanwhile, a Russian drone hit the headquarters of Ukraine's domestic security service (SBU) in Kyiv on Friday.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the strike "a major escalation" of the war.
"Moscow launched this strike during a renewed push for peace — laying bare its true rejection of diplomacy," he wrote on X.
Zelenskyy said he ordered "an appropriate, tangible response and, where possible, one that mirrors this strike."
Ukraine has also launched repeated drone strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and the retail giant Wildberries.
Why Ukraine's books are becoming a casualty of war

articles.title: LTFRB to map out alternative routes when NLEx is congested, flooded
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Saturday said it instructed regional offices to map out alternative routes of major expressways. The order…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Saturday said it instructed regional offices to map out alternative routes of major expressways.
The order was made to prevent traffic build-up during severe floods.
The move followed the recent traffic congestion that occurred along parts of Northern Luzon Expressway (NLEx), where motorists were stranded for nearly eight hours.

Acting LTFRB Chairman Atty. Greg Pua Jr. directed regional offices to coordinate with expressway managements and local government units to identify alternative routes for possible worst-case scenarios, such as floods.
Among the expressways covered by the instruction per region are as follows:

items: Ilocos Region: Tarlac-Pangasinan-La Union Expressway
Metro Manila: Subic-Clark-Tarlac Expressway and NLEx
Calabarzon: South Luzon Expressway, Star Tollway, Cavite-Laguna Expressway and Muntinlupa-Cavite Expressway

blocks.text: “Our priority has always been the welfare of passengers and the delivery of goods to the Filipino people,” Pua said in a statement.
“The incident that happened in NLEX is a wake-up call for us in the LTFRB and other agencies to do our part in coming up with measures to maximize the assistance to the public,” he noted.
The town in San Simon was submerged in waist to thigh-deep floodwaters amid rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or habagat, in recent days.
This situation caused slow-moving traffic along northbound and southbound lanes of NLEx.
As of Saturday, Sept. 5, the road condition in the San Simon interchange area reported light vehicular traffic. /apl

articles.title: Legarda pushes stronger support for PH creative economy
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda called for stronger protection of and investment in Filipino culture and creativity as the country observes Philippine Creative Industries Month this…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Loren Legarda called for stronger protection of and investment in Filipino culture and creativity as the country observes Philippine Creative Industries Month this September, saying economic growth in the sector should translate into sustainable livelihoods and wider opportunities for creative workers.

This year’s celebration carries the theme “We Are a Creative Nation.” Philippine Creative Industries Month is observed every September under Republic Act No. 11904, or the Philippine Creative Industries Development Act, which Legarda authored.
The law promotes the development of Philippine creative industries and recognizes their contribution to nation-building and socioeconomic development.

“Filipino creativity is more than talent to be admired. For many of our fellow Filipinos, it is a job and a livelihood. Our responsibility is to make sure that the people behind our music, films, crafts, designs, stories, food, and traditions are given the support and opportunities they deserve,” Legarda said.

Latest data from the Philippine Statistics Authority showed that the Philippine creative economy reached P2.12 trillion in 2025, up 6.9 percent from P1.98 trillion in 2024 and accounting for 7.6 percent of the country’s gross domestic product.
Creative industries supported 8.71 million jobs, equivalent to 17.8 percent of total employment in the country.

“These figures show how much Filipino creativity already contributes to our economy. But the important question is whether economic growth has reached the very people who create. Does the weaver in the province earn enough from her craft? Can a musician make a living from his original composition? Can a filmmaker, designer, artist, or young creative turn talent into a stable career? Can a local artisan find a market beyond his or her community?” Legarda said.
As chairperson of the Senate Committee on Culture and the Arts, Legarda has pushed to connect cultural preservation with economic opportunities.
She initiated the National Arts and Crafts Fair in 2016, providing a national platform for local artisans and cultural communities to showcase their work, reach consumers, and find wider markets.

“Our artisans should not have to choose between preserving their craft and earning a decent living. When we give them access to markets and opportunities, we help keep traditions alive while allowing families and communities to benefit from the skills and knowledge they have carried for generations,” Legarda said.

Legarda has also filed several cultural measures in the 20th Congress, including Senate Bill No. 817, or the proposed Department of Culture Act; Senate Bill No. 822, or the Philippine Culinary Heritage Act; Senate Bill No. 824, or the Philippine Indigenous Writing Systems Act; Senate Bill No. 826, or the Philippine Music Industry Act; and Senate Bill No. 827, or the Philippine Rondalla Training Program Act.

“A stronger creative economy needs more than recognition. Applause, admiration, and awards are not enough if there is insufficient support to help it thrive. Our artists and cultural workers need institutions that work, laws that protect them, opportunities to develop their skills, and markets where Filipino creativity can grow and compete,” she said.

Legarda has also pushed for the institutionalization and strengthening of the Schools of Living Traditions, including through Senate Bill No. 1507, to support the transmission of indigenous knowledge, skills, practices, and cultural expressions within communities.

“Culture survives because people continue to live it, teach it, create from it, and pass it on. When no one wants to learn weaving, play traditional music, write, or continue an old practice because it no longer provides a livelihood, we gradually lose the very culture we seek to protect. We cannot build a creative economy by allowing the very traditions and knowledge that give Filipino creativity its identity to disappear,” Legarda said.

She added that strengthening the creative sector requires an ecosystem in which artists and creators can develop their skills, protect their work, secure financing, reach bigger markets, and build sustainable careers and enterprises while preserving the Filipino character of their work.

“The Filipino has never lacked imagination or talent. What our creatives need are doors that stay open, with access to training, protection, financing, markets, and institutions that believe in their work,” Legarda said.

“Protecting our culture and building a stronger creative economy are part of the same work, creating better opportunities for our people while ensuring that the knowledge, traditions, and skills that make Filipino creativity distinct continue to have a future,” she added.

articles.title: 2 men sued for alleged theft of steel bars from Angeles creek slope
articles.summary: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — Charges have been filed against two men who were caught allegedly smashing a portion of the Sapang Balen Creek’s concrete slope protection in Barangay San Nicolas, Angeles…

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — Charges have been filed against two men who were caught allegedly smashing a portion of the Sapang Balen Creek’s concrete slope protection in Barangay San Nicolas, Angeles City.

Col. Robert Domingo, officer-in-charge of the Angeles City Police Office, told the Inquirer in a text message Saturday (Sept. 5) that charges of theft and malicious mischief had been filed against the suspects.
Police identified the suspects only as aliases “Ryan,” a resident of Barangay Cutcut, Angeles City, and “Mervin,” from Barangay Manibaug Paralaya in Porac, Pampanga.
On Monday, on its social media page, the Angeles City government condemned the destruction of the slope protection and the alleged theft of its steel bars.

“Amid heavy rains and flooding caused by the southwest monsoon, an incident involving the alleged destruction of a slope protection structure, as well as the cutting and removal of steel bars embedded in it, was reported at Sapang Balen Creek in Barangay San Nicolas, Angeles City,” it said in Filipino.

On Thursday, Angeles City police investigated the incident and learned from Barangay San Nicolas Chairperson Amalia Torres that she personally saw two men cutting and removing steel bars from the slope protection at around 1 p.m. on Aug. 30 amid heavy rain.
“She reportedly confronted the suspects, prompting them to leave the area. However, the suspects allegedly returned after she had left, and continued removing the steel bars,” police said.
The incident was captured on a mobile phone and reported to the Angeles City police on Sept. 2.

Police investigation and a review of the video footage led to the identification of the suspects, who were invited for questioning and confronted by Torres and officials of the Angeles City Engineering Office on Sept. 3.
The Angeles City government urged the public to report suspicious activities along creeks, drainage systems, slope protection structures, and other public infrastructure to the authorities. /apl

articles.title: Critics, Dutertes react to arrest order in VP Sara's grave threats case
articles.summary: After Vice President Sara Duterte asked who would be held accountable if something happened to her following the issuance of an arrest warrant in her grave threats case, Bicol Saro party-list…

blocks.text: Published September 5, 2026 8:24pm

After Vice President Sara Duterte asked who would be held accountable if something happened to her following the issuance of an arrest warrant in her grave threats case, Bicol Saro party-list Representative Terry Ridon on Saturday said she should answer for the allegations against her.
A Quezon City court issued an arrest warrant for Duterte over alleged grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
In front of the Quezon City Hall of Justice on Saturday, before posting bail, Duterte said she did not feel safe.
“I do not feel safe at all. Sinong sasagot kapag namatay ako mamayang gabi? Sinong mananagot?” she said.
(Who will be accountable if I die tonight? Who will be liable?)

“‘Sinong mananagot?’ Kayo po, Madam Vice President, ang kailangang managot at sumagot sa mga alegasyong kinakaharap ninyo. Tama na po ang drama. Wala naman pong grave threats case ngayon kung hindi dahil sa mga pahayag na naging batayan ng kasong isinampa laban sa inyo,” Ridon said in a statement.

(“Who will be accountable?” You, Madam Vice President, need to be accountable and answer for the allegations you are facing. Enough drama. There would be no grave threats case now if not for the statements that became the basis for the case filed against you.)
“Harapin po ninyo ang proseso at ilahad po ninyo ang inyong depensa sa korte,” he added.
(Face the process and present your defense in court.)

Meanwhile, ML Party-list Representative Leila de Lima, who spent five years in detention during former President Rodrigo Duterte’s administration on drug-related charges, said the issuance of the arrest warrant means the court found sufficient basis to examine the evidence against the Vice President.

“VP Sara may not be used to being held accountable, but now she must answer the accusations against her in a criminal court. Hindi na nga dapat tumagal ito (This shouldn’t have taken this long), but at least, it's finally happening,” De Lima said on Friday.
In a separate Facebook post, De Lima asked, “Bakit sila umiiwas at natatakot sa due process?”
(Why are they evading and afraid of due process?)
'Political harassment'
Duterte’s relatives in the House of Representatives defended her and criticized the arrest warrant.
“I am with VP Inday. I am a Filipino, and I don’t feel safe,” Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte said in a Facebook post after his sister posted bail.
In a separate statement, Pulong’s son, Davao City 2nd District Representative Omar Duterte, called the arrest warrant “a clear act of political harassment.”

Omar Duterte likened the case to what was done to former President Rodrigo Duterte, who is currently detained at the International Criminal Court and awaiting trial on crimes against humanity charges in connection with his administration’s war on drugs.
“To the Filipino people, I ask you with all sincerity: please wake up and see what the current administration is doing,” Omar Duterte said. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Rescuers in Nepal pull 2 people alive from the debris 10 days after devastating floods
articles.summary: Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of missing people.

image.caption: A Chinese national is shown after being rescued by soldiers during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project, in Nepal's Rasuwa district, on Saturday. (Nepal Army/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of missing people.
900 workers still missing, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in various tunnels

Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations on Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of missing people.

The man was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post by the country's prime minister's office, bringing the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued on Friday.

Nepal's army said a joint rescue team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre tunnel and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Images showed him being evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.
A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man out of the tunnel.
CCTV shared audio of the man talking to an officer, saying how he repeatedly shouted whenever he saw the rescue crews' lights, but they could not hear him.

items: 2 trapped workers rescued from hydropower tunnel 9 days after Nepal floods

blocks.text: "When they rescued me today, when they shone [the light] before my eyes, I couldn't believe it," he said.
The man was taken to hospital and was in stable condition, according to CCTV.

Rescue efforts have increasingly focused on 12 hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing and roughly 500 are believed to be trapped in various tunnels, authorities said. Specialized rescue teams from India, China, South Korea and the United States have been searching through debris, damaged structures and tunnels at the projects, hoping to find survivors.
2 workers rescued from buried Nepal tunnel
In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal's army spokesperson said Saturday. Officials said she was airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment.
Images released by Nepal's army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house. They gave her bottled water before pulling her to safety, wrapped in a grey blanket.
At least 1,300 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, which were likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal's disaster management agency.
